You have an Azure subscription that contains a Recovery Services vault named Vault1. The subscription includes the virtual machines shown in the following table:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783631013861-jsnbsz7c.png)  
  
You plan to schedule backups to run every night at 23:00.  
  
Which virtual machines can you back up by using Azure Backup?
questions.explanation:
Azure Backup for Azure virtual machines supports the listed server operating systems and supported Linux distributions, including Windows Server 2012 R2, Windows Server 2016, and Ubuntu Server 18.04 LTS. Microsoft Learn’s current support matrix also includes Windows 10 client for Azure VM backup. In addition, Azure VM backup is a platform-level backup operation and a VM being configured for auto-shutdown earlier in the evening does not disqualify it from protection. Therefore VM1, VM2, VM3, and VM4 can all be backed up by Azure Backup.

**Learn more:** [Support matrix for Azure VM backups - Azure Backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-support-matrix-iaas) · [FAQ - Backing up Azure VMs - Azure Backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-azure-vm-backup-faq)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has three offices located in Miami, Los Angeles, and New York. Each office contains a datacenter.  
  
You have an Azure subscription that includes resources in the East US and West US Azure regions. Each region contains a virtual network, and the virtual networks are peered.  
  
You need to connect the datacenters to the subscription. The solution must minimize network latency between the datacenters.  
  
What should you create?

options.text: three Azure Application Gateways and one On-premises data gateway
three virtual hubs and one virtual WAN
three virtual WANs and one virtual hub
three On-premises data gateways and one Azure Application Gateway

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual WAN is the Azure service intended for connecting branch offices and on-premises datacenters to Azure through regional virtual hubs. To minimize latency, each physical site should connect to the nearest Azure region by using its own virtual hub, and multiple hubs in the same Virtual WAN are automatically interconnected over Microsoft's backbone. A single Virtual WAN with three virtual hubs therefore provides low-latency regional access for the three datacenters while preserving connectivity across the environment. Separate Virtual WANs would isolate the hubs from one another, and Application Gateway or On-premises data gateway do not provide this branch-to-Azure network topology.

**Learn more:** [Architecture: Global transit network architecture - Azure Virtual WAN](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/virtual-wan-global-transit-network-architecture) · [What is Azure Virtual WAN?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/virtual-wan-about)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains a virtual machine named VM1 and an Azure function named App1.  
  
You need to create an alert rule that will run App1 if VM1 stops.  
  
What should you create for the alert rule?

options.text: a security group that has dynamic device membership

questions.explanation:
In Azure Monitor, an alert rule triggers an action group when its condition is met. Action groups can perform automated actions such as calling an Azure Function, which is how App1 can run when an alert detects that VM1 has stopped. Microsoft Learn states that alerts initiate the associated action group and that action groups can include Azure functions.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Monitor alerts - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-overview) · [Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups)

You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant that contains 5,000 user accounts.  
  
You create a new user account named AdminUser1.  
  
You need to assign the **User administrator** administrative role to AdminUser1.  
  
What should you do from the user account properties?

options.text: From the Licenses blade, assign a new license
From the Directory role blade, modify the directory role
From the Groups blade, invite the user account to a new group

questions.explanation:
The **User administrator** permission is a built-in Azure AD administrative role, so it is assigned from the user's **Directory role** or assigned roles settings. A license assignment only grants product/service usage rights, and adding or inviting the user to a group does not assign this built-in administrative role in the user properties workflow. Microsoft documentation for assigning Microsoft Entra roles shows that role assignment is performed by selecting the user and assigning the directory role.

**Learn more:** [Assign Azure roles using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/role-assignments-portal) · [Assign administrator and non-administrator roles to users with Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/manage-roles-portal)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant configured for hybrid coexistence with the on-premises Active Directory domain.  
  
You plan to deploy several new virtual machines (VMs) in Azure. The VMs will have the same operating system and custom software requirements.  
  
You configure a reference VM in the on-premises virtual environment and then generalize the VM to create an image.  
  
You need to upload the image to Azure so that it is available for selection when you create the new Azure VMs.  
  
Which PowerShell cmdlets should you use?
questions.explanation:
`Add-AzVhd` is the Azure PowerShell cmdlet used to upload a virtual hard disk from an on-premises machine to Azure. That is the step required to place the generalized image in Azure so it can be used as the basis for new VMs. `Add-AzVM` is for VM configuration/deployment, and `Add-AzImageDataDisk` is only for building an image definition with data disks rather than uploading the source OS image itself. Microsoft Learn documents `Add-AzVhd` as uploading a virtual hard disk from an on-premises machine to Azure, which matches this requirement.

**Learn more:** [Add-AzVhd (Az.Compute) | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.compute/add-azvhd?view=azps-16.0.0) · [Az.Compute Module | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.compute/?view=azps-15.4.0)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Subscription1.  
  
You have 5 TB of data that must be transferred to Subscription1.  
  
You plan to use an Azure Import/Export job.  
  
What can you use as the destination for the imported data?

options.text: the Azure File Sync Storage Sync Service

questions.explanation:
Azure Import/Export supports importing data by shipping drives to an Azure datacenter, and the supported targets are Azure Blob storage and Azure Files. Of the listed choices, only Azure File Storage corresponds to Azure Files, so it is the valid destination for the imported data.

**Learn more:** [Using Azure Import/Export to transfer data to and from Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/import-export/storage-import-export-service) · [Tutorial to transfer data to Azure Files with Azure Import/Export](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/import-export/storage-import-export-data-to-files)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two Azure subscriptions named **Sub1** and **Sub2**.  
  
An administrator creates a custom role that has an assignable scope set to a resource group named **RG1** in **Sub1**.  
  
You need to ensure that you can apply the custom role to any resource group in **Sub1** and **Sub2**. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Select the custom role and add Sub1 and Sub2 to the assignable scopes. Remove RG1 from the assignable scopes.
Create a new custom role for Sub1. Create a new custom role for Sub2. Remove the role from RG1.
Create a new custom role for Sub1 and add Sub2 to the assignable scopes. Remove the role from RG1.
Select the custom role and add Sub1 to the assignable scopes. Remove RG1 from the assignable scopes. Create a new custom role for Sub2.

questions.explanation:
In Azure RBAC, a custom role is assignable only within its defined `AssignableScopes`. If the scope is a resource group, the role can be assigned only at that resource group or below. To use the same custom role for any resource group in both subscriptions, the role definition must include **Sub1** and **Sub2** in `AssignableScopes`. At subscription scope, the role becomes available for assignment to any resource group within that subscription. Using one updated role definition is less administrative work than creating separate custom roles for each subscription.

**Learn more:** [Understand Azure role definitions - Azure RBAC | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/role-definitions) · [Azure custom roles - Azure RBAC | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/custom-roles)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Storage account named `storage1`.  
  
For `storage1`, you create an encryption scope named `Scope1`.  
  
Which storage types can you encrypt by using `Scope1`?

options.text: file shares, containers, and tables only
file shares, containers, tables, and queues

questions.explanation:
Azure Storage encryption scopes apply to Blob storage only. An encryption scope can be assigned at the container level as a default and used for blobs within that container, but it does not apply to Azure Files, Table storage, or Queue storage. Therefore, the only storage type in the options that can be encrypted by using the scope is containers.

**Learn more:** [Encryption scopes for Blob storage - Azure Storage | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/encryption-scope-overview) · [Create and manage encryption scopes - Azure Storage | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/encryption-scope-manage)

You have an Azure web app named App1. App1 has the deployment slots shown in the following table:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783630248313-kneeyq1l.png)  
  
In webapp1-test, you validate several changes to App1.  
  
You back up App1.  
  
You swap webapp1-test with webapp1-prod and discover that App1 is having performance issues.  
  
You need to return to the previous version of App1 as quickly as possible.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation: Azure App Service deployment slot swaps are reversible by performing another swap between the same slots. Because the previous production version remains in the other slot after the first swap, swapping the slots again is the quickest way to restore the earlier production deployment. Backup restore is slower and is not the fastest rollback method for a failed slot swap.

questions.explanation:

You plan to deploy the Azure container instances shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783643029016-f4qq0ux7.png)  
  
Which instances can you deploy to a container group?
questions.explanation: Azure Container Instances container groups support only a single operating system type (Windows or Linux) across all containers in the group. Multiple containers per group is currently a Linux-only feature. Therefore, only Linux containers can be deployed together in a single container group, making instances 3 and 4 (the Linux containers) the valid combination.

You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783646372348-40msfbvi.png)  
  
You need to create a single Azure Resource Manager (ARM) template that will be used to deploy the resources.  
  
Which resource should be included in the `dependsOn` section for VM1?
questions.explanation: In an ARM template, an Azure virtual machine must depend on the network interface that is attached to it, because the VM references that NIC in its `networkProfile` and cannot be provisioned until the NIC exists. Related resources such as the virtual network, public IP address, and network security group are typically dependencies of the NIC resource rather than direct dependencies of the virtual machine.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to deploy route-based Site-to-Site VPN connections between several on-premises locations and an Azure virtual network.  
  
Which tunneling protocol should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure route-based Site-to-Site VPN gateways use IPsec/IKE with IKEv2 for these connections. Microsoft Learn states that when connecting to Azure route-based VPN gateways, the on-premises VPN devices must support IKEv2. PPTP and L2TP are remote-access protocols rather than the protocol used for Azure route-based S2S VPN gateways, and IKEv1 is not the correct choice for this route-based multi-site design.

**Learn more:** [Connect VPN gateways to multiple on-premises policy-based VPN devices - Azure VPN Gateway | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/vpn-gateway-connect-multiple-policybased-rm-ps) · [Azure VPN Gateway configuration settings | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/vpn-gateway-about-vpn-gateway-settings)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a main office in London that contains 100 client computers.  
  
Three years ago, you migrated to Azure Active Directory (Azure AD).  
  
The company's security policy states that all personal devices and corporate-owned devices must be registered or joined to Azure AD.  
  
A remote user named User1 is unable to join a personal device to Azure AD from a home network.  
  
You verify that User1 was able to join devices to Azure AD in the past.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can join the device to Azure AD.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Assign the User administrator role to User1.
From the Device settings blade, modify the Maximum number of devices per user setting.
Create a point-to-site VPN from the home network of User1 to Azure.
From the Device settings blade, modify the Users may join devices to Azure AD setting.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra device settings distinguish between whether users are permitted to join devices and how many devices each user can join or register. Because User1 was able to join devices previously, the issue is unlikely to be the general permission to join devices. A common blocker is that the user has reached the tenant's configured device limit. Modifying **Maximum number of devices per user** allows the user to join an additional personal device.

**Learn more:** [Manage devices in Microsoft Entra ID using the Microsoft Entra admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/manage-device-identities) · [Error (The maximum number of devices that can be joined to the workplace by the user has been reached) during a Workplace Join](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/entra/entra-id/ad-dmn-services/maximum-number-of-devices-joined-workplace)

options.text: Configure a DNS name for VM1.

questions.explanation:
Azure Desired State Configuration is enabled on an Azure virtual machine by installing and using a VM extension. VM extensions can only be provisioned when the VM is running and the Azure VM Agent inside the guest can communicate with Azure. Because VM1 is shown as **Stopped (deallocated)**, the required first step is to start the virtual machine before enabling DSC. You have an Azure subscription that contains the resources shown in the following table.

You need to assign Workspace1 a role that allows read, write, and delete operations for the data stored in the containers of storage1.  
  
Which role should you assign?
questions.explanation:
For Azure Storage data in blob containers, the required permission must be a data-plane RBAC role. **Storage Blob Data Contributor** is the built-in role that grants read, write, and delete access to blob containers and blobs. Roles such as **Contributor** and **Storage Account Contributor** manage the storage account resource itself but do not grant direct access to the data in the account's containers, and **Reader and Data Access** does not provide write or delete permissions.

**Learn more:** [Azure built-in roles - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles) · [Access control model for Azure Data Lake Storage - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/data-lake-storage-access-control-model)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named **Subscription1** that contains a virtual network named **VNet1**. **VNet1** is in a resource group named **RG1**.  
  
A user named **User1** has the following roles for **Subscription1**:  
  
- **Reader**  
- **Security Admin**  
- **Security Reader**  
  
You need to ensure that **User1** can assign the **Reader** role for **VNet1** to other users.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Remove User1 from the Security Reader and Reader roles for Subscription1. Assign User1 the Contributor role for Subscription1.
Assign User1 the Contributor role for VNet1.
Assign User1 the Owner role for VNet1.
Assign User1 the Network Contributor role for RG1.

questions.explanation: In Azure RBAC, assigning a role to other users requires permission to create role assignments at the target scope, which is the `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write` action. The built-in **Owner** role includes access delegation and can create role assignments, while **Contributor**, **Network Contributor**, **Reader**, **Security Admin**, and **Security Reader** do not grant role-assignment permission. Assigning **Owner** at the **VNet1** scope gives User1 the ability to assign the **Reader** role for that virtual network without granting broader ownership over the entire subscription.

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains a virtual machine named VM1.  
  
You plan to deploy an Azure Monitor alert rule that will trigger an alert when CPU usage on VM1 exceeds 80 percent.  
  
You need to ensure that the alert rule sends an email message to two users named User1 and User2.  
  
What should you create for Azure Monitor?
questions.explanation: In Azure Monitor, notifications for an alert rule are defined by an action group. An action group can include email receivers, so configuring User1 and User2 in an action group allows the CPU alert for VM1 to send email when the threshold is exceeded. Mail-enabled security groups, distribution groups, and Microsoft 365 groups are directory or messaging objects, not the Azure Monitor alert notification resource.

What should you create for Azure Monitor?

options.text: VM1, VM2, VM3, VMA, VMB, and VMC
VM1, VM3, VMA, and VMC only

questions.explanation:
Azure Backup can protect Azure virtual machines only when the VM is in the same subscription and the same Azure region as the Recovery Services vault; the VM can be in a different resource group from the vault. Because Vault1 is in **West Europe**, the VMs in **West Europe** are eligible: **VM1, VM3, VMA, and VMC**. The **North Europe** VMs (**VM2** and **VMB**) are not eligible for backup to Vault1.

**Learn more:** [Back Up Azure VMs in a Recovery Services Vault - Azure Backup | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-azure-arm-vms-prepare) · [Create and configure Recovery Services vaults - Azure Backup | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-create-rs-vault)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named `contoso.com` and an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster named `AKS1`.  
  
An administrator reports that she can't grant access to `AKS1` to the users in `contoso.com`.  
  
You need to ensure that access to `AKS1` can be granted to the `contoso.com` users.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From contoso.com, modify the Organization relationships settings.
From contoso.com, create an OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoint.

questions.explanation:
In this scenario, AKS1 was evidently created without Azure AD (Microsoft Entra ID) integration configured, and legacy AKS-to-Azure-AD integration can only be established when the cluster is created, not retrofitted onto an already-running cluster. The only listed option that actually establishes tenant-based authentication for the cluster is to recreate AKS1 with Azure AD integration enabled; modifying organization relationships, creating an OAuth 2.0 endpoint (Azure AD already exposes OAuth2 endpoints automatically), or adding a namespace do not grant contoso.com users cluster access.

**Learn more:** [Cluster authentication concepts in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/concepts-cluster-authentication)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Solution: You use the Azure portal to modify the **grant control** of the Azure AD conditional access policy.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Changing Conditional Access grant controls is where the MFA requirement is configured, but the policy requirement for an **Azure AD-joined device** is not satisfied by a standard grant-control setting in Azure AD Conditional Access. Microsoft Learn documents grant controls such as requiring multifactor authentication, requiring a device to be marked as compliant, and requiring a Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device. Because the stated goal specifically requires an Azure AD-joined device, altering the grant control alone does not fulfill that requirement.

**Learn more:** [How to Configure Grant Controls in Microsoft Entra - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-in/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-grant) · [What is a Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device? - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/concept-hybrid-join)

questions.question:
Solution: You go to the multi-factor authentication page to change the user settings.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation: Altering settings on the multi-factor authentication page does not configure an Azure AD Conditional Access policy. Conditional Access is required to combine multiple access controls and conditions such as targeting Global Administrators, limiting the requirement to untrusted locations, requiring multifactor authentication, and requiring the device to be Microsoft Entra ID joined. User-level MFA settings alone cannot satisfy those Conditional Access and device-based requirements.

questions.question:
Solution: You go to the multi-factor authentication page to change the user settings.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Requiring multifactor authentication and a Microsoft Entra joined or hybrid joined/compliant device is configured with Conditional Access **grant controls**. Session controls govern post-authentication session restrictions and monitoring, not the access requirements that determine whether sign-in is allowed. Because the requirement is to enforce MFA and device state for administrators from untrusted locations, altering session control does not achieve that policy outcome.

**Learn more:** [How to Configure Grant Controls in Microsoft Entra - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-in/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-grant) · [Conditional Access: Manage Session Controls Effectively - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-session)

questions.question:
You create an Azure Storage account named `contosostorage`.  
  
You plan to create a file share named `data`.  
  
Users need to map a drive to the `data` file share from home computers that run Windows 10.  
  
Which outbound port should be opened between the home computers and the `data` file share?
questions.explanation: Azure file shares are mapped from Windows clients by using SMB, and SMB traffic to Azure Files uses TCP port 445. Therefore, home computers that need to map the `data` share must be allowed outbound access on port 445.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure virtual machine named **VM1**.  
  
You use Azure Backup to create a backup of **VM1** named **Backup1**.  
  
After creating **Backup1**, you make the following changes to **VM1**:  
  
- Modify the size of **VM1**.  
- Copy a file named **Budget.xls** to a folder named **Data**.  
- Reset the password for the built-in administrator account.  
- Add a data disk to **VM1**.  
  
An administrator uses the **Replace existing** option to restore **VM1** from **Backup1**.  
  
You need to ensure that all the changes to **VM1** are restored.  
  
Which change should you perform again?

options.text: Reset the password for the built-in administrator account.

questions.explanation:
When 'Replace existing' is used to restore an Azure VM, Azure Backup replaces the VM's current disks with the disks from the selected recovery point, and per Microsoft's documented behavior the resulting VM's disk count reflects only the recovery point's configuration; a data disk that was added to the VM after Backup1 was taken is therefore not part of the recovery point and is not present after the restore, so it must be added again.

**Learn more:** [Restore VMs by using the Azure portal using Azure Backup - Azure Backup | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-azure-arm-restore-vms)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription named **Subscription1**.  
  
You have **5 TB** of data that you need to transfer to **Subscription1**.  
  
You plan to use an **Azure Import/Export** job.  
  
What can you use as the destination for the imported data?
questions.explanation:
Azure Import/Export supports importing data by shipping disk drives to an Azure datacenter, and the supported destinations are Azure Blob storage and Azure Files. Of the listed options, only Azure File Storage is a valid destination for imported data.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Import/Export documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/import-export/) · [Using Azure Import/Export to transfer data to and from Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/import-export/storage-import-export-service)

questions.question:
Your company has an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to deploy several Azure virtual machines (VMs) by using Azure Resource Manager (ARM) templates. You have been told that the VMs will be part of a single availability set.  
  
You must ensure that the ARM template you configure allows as many VMs as possible to remain accessible if fabric failure or maintenance occurs.  
  
Which value should you configure for the `platformUpdateDomainCount` property?
questions.explanation: In an Azure availability set, update domains define groups of VMs and underlying physical resources that can be rebooted together during planned maintenance. Increasing the update domain count spreads VMs across more groups, so fewer VMs are affected at one time. Azure supports a maximum of 20 update domains for an availability set, so configuring `platformUpdateDomainCount` to 20 allows the greatest number of VMs to remain available.

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription named **Subscription1** that contains an Azure Log Analytics workspace named **Workspace1**.  
  
You need to view the error events from a table named **Event**.  
  
Which query should you run in **Workspace1**?
questions.explanation: Azure Log Analytics queries use Kusto Query Language (KQL), which starts with a table name followed by pipe operators for filtering and searching. The syntax `Event | search \"error\"` correctly queries the Event table for records containing \"error\". SQL syntax (option A) is invalid for KQL, the `is` operator (option C) is not valid equality syntax in KQL (should be `==`), and PowerShell cmdlets (option D) are not used in Log Analytics queries.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains a storage account named `account1`.  
  
You plan to upload the disk files of a virtual machine to `account1` from your on-premises network. The on-premises network uses a public IP address space of `131.107.1.0/24`.  
  
You plan to use the disk files to provision an Azure virtual machine named `VM1`. `VM1` will be attached to a virtual network named `VNet1`. `VNet1` uses an IP address space of `192.168.0.0/24`.  
  
You need to configure `account1` to meet the following requirements:  
  
- Ensure that you can upload the disk files to `account1`.  
- Ensure that you can attach the disks to `VM1`.  
- Prevent all other access to `account1`.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: From the Networking blade of account1, select Selected networks.
From the Networking blade of account1, select Allow trusted Microsoft services to access this storage account.
From the Networking blade of account1, add the 131.107.1.0/24 IP address range.
From the Networking blade of account1, add VNet1.
From the Service endpoints blade of VNet1, add a service endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Learn states that Azure Storage firewall network rules apply only to data-plane REST access to blobs and do not affect virtual machine disk traffic, including disk mount and attach operations. Restricting account1's networking to Selected networks and adding the on-premises range 131.107.1.0/24 as an allowed IP rule permits the disk-file upload from on-premises while blocking all other access; VM1 can still attach the resulting disk without any additional virtual network rule or service endpoint, since that traffic isn't gated by the storage firewall at all.

**Learn more:** [Guidelines and limitations: Azure Storage firewall | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-network-security-limitations)

questions.question:
Solution: You create a packet capture from Azure Network Watcher.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Network Watcher packet capture can remotely capture packet-level traffic to and from an Azure virtual machine, which allows inspection of traffic flowing from VM1 to VM2. A three-hour capture is supported because packet capture sessions can run for a user-defined duration up to several days. That makes this an appropriate way to inspect the required traffic.\
\
**Learn more:** [Packet Capture Overview - Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/packet-capture-overview) · [Start, stop, download, and delete packet captures with Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/packet-capture-manage)

questions.question:
Solution: From Azure Network Watcher, you create a connection monitor.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A Connection Monitor in Azure Network Watcher is used to monitor connectivity between endpoints, including reachability and performance metrics such as latency. It does not capture and inspect all packets exchanged between VM1 and VM2. To inspect all network traffic for a limited period such as three hours, the appropriate Network Watcher capability is packet capture.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Network Watcher Connection Monitor overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/network-watcher/connection-monitor-overview) · [Manage packet captures for virtual machines with Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/network-watcher/network-watcher-packet-capture-manage-portal)

questions.question:
Solution: From Performance Monitor, you create a Data Collector Set (DCS).  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation: A Performance Monitor Data Collector Set gathers system performance data such as counters, traces, and logs from Windows, but it is not a packet-inspection solution for capturing all traffic exchanged between two virtual machines. Inspecting all network traffic from VM1 to VM2 for a defined period requires packet capture functionality, such as Azure Network Watcher packet capture or another packet-sniffing tool on the VMs. Therefore, creating a DCS does not meet the stated requirement.

questions.question:
Solution: In Azure Monitor, you create a metric for **Network In** and **Network Out**.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Network In and Network Out metrics in Azure Monitor show aggregate traffic measurements, not the contents or full packet-level details of communications between VM1 and VM2. Inspecting all traffic for a three-hour window requires Azure Network Watcher packet capture, which is specifically designed to capture and analyze traffic to and from Azure virtual machines and can be time-bounded and filtered as needed.\
\
**Learn more:** [Inspect and analyze Network Watcher packet capture files - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/packet-capture-inspect) · [Start, stop, download, and delete packet captures with Azure Network Watcher - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/packet-capture-manage)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have five Azure virtual machines that run Windows Server 2016. The virtual machines are configured as web servers.  
  
You have an Azure load balancer named LB1 that provides load-balancing services for the virtual machines.  
  
You need to ensure that visitors are served by the same web server for each request.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: Session persistence to Client IP and protocol
Floating IP (direct server return) to Enabled

questions.explanation:
Azure Load Balancer uses session persistence to keep requests from the same client directed to the same backend instance. Microsoft Learn states that **Client IP and protocol** means successive requests from the same client IP address and protocol combination are handled by the same virtual machine. By contrast, **None** uses the default hash-based distribution, **Idle Time-out** only affects inactive connections, and **Floating IP** is unrelated to session affinity.

**Learn more:** [Azure Load Balancer distribution modes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/distribution-mode-concepts) · [Configure Azure Load Balancer distribution mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/load-balancer-distribution-mode)

Your company has an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant configured for hybrid coexistence with the on-premises Active Directory domain.  
  
The on-premises virtual environment contains virtual machines (VMs) that run on Windows Server 2012 R2 Hyper-V host servers.  
  
You created PowerShell scripts to automate the configuration of newly created VMs, and you plan to create several additional VMs.  
  
You need a solution that ensures the scripts run on the new VMs.  
  
Which of the following is the best solution?

options.text: Configure a SetupComplete.cmd batch file in the %windir%\setup\scripts directory.
Configure a Group Policy Object (GPO) to run the scripts as logon scripts.
Configure a Group Policy Object (GPO) to run the scripts as startup scripts.
Place the scripts in a new virtual hard disk (VHD).

questions.explanation: A computer startup script deployed through Group Policy is the best fit because it runs automatically when a domain-joined VM starts, without requiring a user to sign in. That makes it the appropriate centralized mechanism for ensuring configuration scripts execute on newly created VMs in an on-premises Active Directory environment. Logon scripts depend on user logon, SetupComplete.cmd is tied to Windows setup on an individual machine rather than ongoing domain management, and placing scripts in a VHD does not cause them to run.

You have an Azure subscription that contains the resources in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783631011637-33r20i35.png)  
  
VM1 and VM2 are deployed from the same template and host line-of-business applications.  
  
You configure the network security group (NSG) shown in the exhibit. (Click the Exhibit tab.)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783631014571-3dj4j6sc.jpg)  
  
You need to prevent users of VM1 and VM2 from accessing websites on the Internet over TCP port 80.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Disassociate the NSG from a network interface
Change the Port_80 inbound security rule.
Change the DenyWebSites outbound security rule.

questions.explanation:
In Azure, blocking users on virtual machines from reaching websites over TCP port 80 requires an **outbound** NSG rule that denies destination **Internet** on port **80**, and that NSG must be associated with the subnet or the VMs' network interfaces for the rule to take effect. The configured **DenyWebSites** outbound rule already matches that requirement, but because the NSG is not associated with any subnet or NIC, it is not applied. Associating the NSG to **Subnet1** applies the deny rule to both VM1 and VM2 because both virtual machines are deployed in that subnet. Official Microsoft documentation states that NSG rules filter inbound and outbound traffic only for associated subnets or network interfaces.

**Learn more:** [How Network Security Groups Filter Network Traffic in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/network-security-group-how-it-works) · [Tutorial: Filter network traffic with a network security group (NSG)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/tutorial-filter-network-traffic)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains a storage account named `storage1` in the North Europe Azure region.  
  
You need to ensure that when blob data is added to `storage1`, a secondary copy is created in the East US region. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Azure Blob object replication asynchronously copies block blobs from a source storage account to a destination storage account, including across regions, so it is the feature intended for creating a secondary copy in a specific target region such as East US. Geo-redundant storage does replicate to another region, but Azure selects the paired secondary region and that region cannot be changed, so it does not satisfy a requirement for East US specifically. Operational backup and lifecycle management do not provide cross-region blob replication.

**Learn more:** [Configure object replication - Azure Storage | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/object-replication-configure) · [Data redundancy - Azure Storage | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-redundancy)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure virtual machine (VM) with a single data disk attached. You have been assigned to attach this data disk to another Azure VM.  
  
You need to ensure that your approach keeps the virtual machines offline for the minimum possible amount of time.  
  
Which action should you take **FIRST**?

options.text: Stop the VM that includes the data disk.
Stop the VM that the data disk must be attached to.
Delete the VM that includes the data disk.

questions.explanation:
An Azure managed data disk must be detached from its current VM before it can be attached to another VM, and Azure supports hot detach for data disks, which helps minimize downtime. Stopping or deleting a VM is not the required first step for moving a data disk between VMs, and the destination VM does not need to be stopped first just to receive the disk.

**Learn more:** [Detach a data disk from a Windows VM - Azure Virtual Machines | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/detach-disk) · [Attach a data disk to a Windows VM with PowerShell | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/attach-disk-ps)

You need to manage outbound traffic from VNET1 by using Firewall1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Upgrade ASP1 to the Premium SKU.

questions.explanation: Managing outbound traffic through Azure Firewall requires routing the traffic to the firewall. In Azure, that is done by creating a user-defined route in a route table and associating it to the relevant subnet so outbound packets use the firewall as the next hop. The other options do not establish traffic steering through Azure Firewall.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two Azure virtual networks named VNet1 and VNet2. VNet1 contains an Azure virtual machine named VM1. VNet2 contains an Azure virtual machine named VM2.  
  
VM1 hosts a frontend application that connects to VM2 to retrieve data.  
  
Users report that the frontend application is performing more slowly than usual.  
  
You need to view the average round-trip time (RTT) of packets from VM1 to VM2.  
  
Which Azure Network Watcher feature should you use?
questions.explanation:
Connection monitor is the Azure Network Watcher feature for monitoring connectivity between endpoints and reporting latency metrics, including round-trip time (RTT). Microsoft Learn documents that Connection monitor provides round-trip time data and Azure Monitor metrics such as RoundTripTimeMs and AverageRoundtripMs for probes sent between a source and destination. IP flow verify only determines whether a packet is allowed or denied, Connection troubleshoot is primarily a point-in-time diagnostic test, and NSG flow logs record flow activity rather than RTT metrics.

**Learn more:** [Connection Monitor Overview - Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/connection-monitor-overview) · [Supported metrics - Microsoft.Network/networkWatchers/connectionMonitors - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/microsoft-network-networkwatchers-connectionmonitors-metrics)

You have a deployment template named **Template1** that is used to deploy **10 Azure web apps**.  
  
You need to identify what must be deployed before you deploy **Template1**. The solution must **minimize Azure costs**.  
  
What should you identify?
questions.explanation: Azure web apps are deployed into an App Service plan, which provides the compute resources they run on. Multiple web apps can share the same App Service plan, so using a single plan for all 10 apps minimizes cost compared with creating multiple plans. Azure Application Gateway and Azure Traffic Manager are traffic distribution services and are not required just to host the web apps.

questions.question:
Solution: From the **Subscriptions** blade, you select the subscription, and then click **Programmatic deployment**.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation: The **Programmatic deployment** option at the subscription level is used to access automation and template deployment information, not to view the creation date and time of resources in a specific resource group such as RG1. To determine when resources in RG1 were created, you would need resource-group-specific deployment history, activity log details, or resource metadata rather than the subscription's Programmatic deployment entry.

questions.question:
Solution: From the **RG1** blade, you select **Deployments**.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation: The **Deployments** view in an Azure resource group displays the history of ARM template deployments and their timestamps, not the creation date and time for each resource in the resource group. A deployment time is not the same as an individual resource creation timestamp, so using **Deployments** does not directly meet the requirement to view when the resources were created.

questions.question:
Solution: From the **RG1** blade, you select **Automation script**.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Selecting **Automation script** does not show when the resources in the resource group were created. In Azure Resource Manager, the relevant place for creation timing of template-deployed resources is the resource group's **Deployments** history, which records deployments and their timestamps. **Automation script** is for generating an automation template/script for the existing resources, not for viewing their creation date and time.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use the Azure portal and Azure Resource Manager to Manage Resource Groups - Azure Resource Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/manage-resource-groups-portal)

questions.question:
Solution: From the **Subscriptions** blade, you select the subscription, and then click **Resource providers**.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
The **Resource providers** page shows which Azure resource providers and types are available or registered for a subscription; it does not show creation timestamps for resources. To determine when resources in **RG1** were created, you use **Azure Activity Log**, which records subscription-level and resource group-level management events such as resource creation and includes the event time.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure resource providers and types - Azure Resource Manager | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/resource-providers-and-types) · [Azure Monitor activity log - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/platform/activity-log)

You have an Azure subscription that contains the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783630269235-kl1nr5ge.png)  
  
You need to configure a proximity placement group for VMSS1.  

Which proximity placement groups should you use?
questions.explanation: A proximity placement group can be associated only with compute resources that are deployed in the same Azure region. Because VMSS1 is located in **West US**, the only eligible proximity placement group is **Proximity2**, which is also in **West US**. Proximity1 and Proximity3 are in **Central US**, so they cannot be assigned to VMSS1.

You need to ensure that Bastion1 can support 100 concurrent SSH users. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Upgrade Bastion1 to the Standard SKU

questions.explanation:
Azure Bastion increases concurrent SSH capacity by using host scaling, but host scaling is available only on the Standard SKU or higher. Bastion1 is currently on the Basic SKU, so the prerequisite first step is to upgrade it to Standard. The subnet is already /26, which satisfies the subnet sizing needed for host scaling, so resizing the subnet is not the first action.

Admin1 tries to deploy an Azure Marketplace resource by using an Azure Resource Manager template. Admin1 deploys the template by using Azure PowerShell and receives the following error message:

To accept legal terms, please go to the Azure portal (http://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=534873) and configure programmatic deployment for the Marketplace item or create it there for the first time.`  
  
You need to ensure that Admin1 can deploy the Marketplace resource successfully.

options.text: From Azure PowerShell, run the Set-AzApiManagementSubscription cmdlet
From the Azure portal, register the Microsoft.Marketplace resource provider

From the Azure portal, assign the Billing administrator role to Admin1

questions.explanation:
Azure Marketplace offers that require purchase validation must have their legal terms accepted once per subscription before they can be deployed programmatically with ARM templates or PowerShell. The Az.MarketplaceOrdering cmdlet `Set-AzMarketplaceTerms` is specifically used to accept those terms for the publisher, product, and plan, which resolves the validation error and allows deployment to proceed.

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains a storage account. The account stores website data.  
  
You need to ensure that inbound user traffic uses the Microsoft point-of-presence (POP) closest to the user's location.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation: Azure Storage routing preference controls how client traffic is routed to the public endpoint. Selecting the Microsoft global network option causes inbound traffic to enter the Microsoft network through the POP closest to the user, which is the specific requirement here. Private endpoints restrict access privately, Azure Firewall rules filter traffic, and load balancing does not provide this storage routing behavior.

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains a storage account. The account stores website data.  
  
You need to ensure that inbound user traffic uses the Microsoft point-of-presence (POP) closest to the user's location.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Customer-managed keys are the correct choice because Azure managed disks can use a customer-managed key stored in Azure Key Vault through a Disk Encryption Set, and that protection applies to both OS disks and data disks. Since the encryption is applied to the managed disks themselves, the disks remain encrypted at rest rather than only while running on a host. Confidential disk encryption does not meet the requirement because it is limited to the OS disk, and encryption at host mainly extends protection to host-side caches and temp storage rather than serving as the primary persisted disk-encryption method by itself. Azure Disk Encryption uses BitLocker or DM-Crypt inside the guest and integrates with Key Vault, but for this requirement set the managed-disk customer-managed key model is the best match.

**Learn more:** [Overview of managed disk encryption options - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/disk-encryption-overview) · [Server-side encryption of Azure managed disks - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/disk-encryption)

You have an Azure virtual machine named VM1.  
  
The network interface for VM1 is configured as shown in the exhibit. (Click the Exhibit tab.)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783632898550-wbdq8y0z.jpg)  
  
You deploy a web server on VM1, and then create a secure website that is accessible by using the HTTPS protocol. VM1 is used as a web server only.  
  
You need to make sure that users can connect to the website from the Internet.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: For Rule5, change the Action to Allow and change the priority to 401
Create a new inbound rule that allows TCP protocol 443 and configure the rule to have a priority of 501.

questions.explanation:
Azure network security group inbound rules are processed in ascending priority order, and the first matching rule is applied. HTTPS requires inbound TCP port 443 to be allowed from the Internet. In the shown rules, TCP 443 is explicitly denied by Rule2 at priority 500, so any lower-priority rule cannot override it. Changing Rule5 to Allow with priority 401 places a matching allow rule for port 443 before the deny, which permits Internet clients to reach the secure website.

**Learn more:** [Azure network security groups overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/network-security-groups-overview)

questions.question:
You need to add VM1 and VM2 to the backend pool of LB1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Redeploy VM1 and VM2 to the same availability zone.
Redeploy VM1 and VM2 to the same availability set.
Create a new NSG and associate the NSG to VNET1/Subnet1.

questions.explanation: Azure Load Balancer backend pool members must be reachable through NICs that are attached to the appropriate virtual network for the load balancer. Neither placing the virtual machines in the same availability zone nor the same availability set is required to add them to a backend pool, and creating an NSG does not make a VM eligible for backend pool membership. The necessary first step is to connect VM2 to VNET1/Subnet1 so it can be associated with LB1’s backend pool.

questions.question:
You need to add VM1 and VM2 to the backend pool of LB1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Assign the Owner role to the developers
Assign the Website Contributor role to the developers

questions.explanation:
Azure App Service publishing access is controlled through deployment credentials plus Azure RBAC. Microsoft Learn specifies that a user must have at least Contributor-level permissions on the app to publish, and explicitly includes the built-in **Website Contributor** role. That role grants the necessary publish rights without the broader permissions of **Owner**, so it is the least-privileged option that enables the developers to deploy.

**Learn more:** [Manage deployment credentials - Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/deploy-configure-credentials) · [Azure built-in roles for Web and Mobile - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/web-and-mobile)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Storage account named `storage1`.  
  
You plan to use AzCopy to copy data to `storage1`.  
  
You need to determine which storage services in `storage1` can be targets for the copied data.  
  
Which storage services should you identify?
questions.explanation: AzCopy supports transferring data with Azure Blob storage and Azure Files. Azure Table storage and Queue storage are not supported as general AzCopy copy destinations, so the applicable storage services in the account are only blob and file.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an app named App1 that runs on an Azure web app named webapp1.  
  
The developers at your company upload an update of App1 to a Git repository named Git1.  
  
Webapp1 has the deployment slots shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783637460509-avw5ivaf.png)  
  
You need to ensure that the App1 update is tested before the update is made available to users.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Deploy the App1 update to webapp1-prod, and then test the update
Deploy the App1 update to webapp1-test, and then test the update

questions.explanation:
Azure App Service deployment slots are intended for this exact release pattern: deploy the new version to a nonproduction slot such as **Staging**, test it there, and then **swap** the staging slot with the production slot to promote the tested version to users with minimal downtime. Because **webapp1-test** is the staging slot and **webapp1-prod** is the production slot, the update should be deployed and validated in **webapp1-test**, then the slots should be swapped.

**Learn more:** [Set up staging environments in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/deploy-staging-slots)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure virtual machine named VM1.  
  
Azure collects events from VM1.  
  
You are creating an alert rule in Azure Monitor to notify an administrator when an error is recorded in the **System** event log of VM1.  
  
Which target resource should you monitor in the alert rule?
questions.explanation:
Windows event log entries from a virtual machine are queried as log data in Azure Monitor Logs after they are collected into a Log Analytics workspace. An alert for an error in the System event log is therefore a log search alert that targets the Log Analytics workspace containing that data. The virtual machine resource is used for resource metrics, while a VM extension is not the alert target, and a metric alert is an alert type rather than a target resource.

**Learn more:** [Create Azure Monitor log search alert rules - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-create-log-alert-rule) · [Tutorial: Create a log search alert for an Azure resource - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/tutorial-log-alert)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Recovery Services vault named RSV1. RSV1 has a backup policy that retains instant snapshots for five days and daily backup for 14 days.  
  
RSV1 performs daily backups of VM1. VM1 hosts a static website that was updated eight days ago.  
  
You need to recover VM1 to a point eight days ago. The solution must minimize downtime.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Restore VM1 by using the Replace existing restore configuration option.
Restore VM1 by using the Create new restore configuration option.

questions.explanation:
An eight-day-old recovery point is outside the five-day instant snapshot retention window, so recovery must use a vault recovery point from the daily backups. To minimize downtime, restore the backup as a new VM first rather than replacing the existing VM in place. In-place replacement modifies the production VM and is used to overwrite the existing disks, while creating a new VM brings up a recovered copy without taking the current VM offline first.

**Learn more:** [FAQ - Backing up Azure VMs - Azure Backup | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-azure-vm-backup-faq) · [Support matrix for Azure VM backups - Azure Backup | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-au/azure/backup/backup-support-matrix-iaas)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure App Service web app named App1.  
  
You need to gather performance traces for App1.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: the Diagnose and solve problems settings

questions.explanation:
Azure Application Insights Profiler is the App Service feature designed to capture detailed performance traces and identify slow code paths. Microsoft Learn explicitly says you can enable Application Insights Profiler to start capturing detailed performance traces for Azure App Service apps. The Activity log is for Azure resource events, Deployment Center is for deployment workflows, and Diagnose and solve problems is a troubleshooting entry point rather than the trace-collection feature itself.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot slow app performance issues in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/app-service/troubleshoot-performance-degradation) · [Enable Application Insights Profiler for .NET for Azure App Service apps in Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/profiler/profiler)

options.text: an Azure Key Vault and an access policy
an Azure Storage account and an access policy
a Recovery Services vault and a backup policy
Azure Active Directory (AD) Identity Protection and an Azure policy

questions.explanation:
Azure Key Vault is the Azure service for storing secrets such as passwords, and ARM templates can reference a secret from Key Vault instead of placing the VM administrator password directly in the template or parameter file. Granting the deployment access to the vault allows the secret to be retrieved securely during deployment, which satisfies the requirement to avoid plain-text password storage.

**Learn more:** [Key Vault secret with template - Azure Resource Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/templates/key-vault-parameter) · [Secrets documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/secrets/)

You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant linked to 10 Azure subscriptions.  
  
You need to monitor user activity centrally across all the subscriptions.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
A Log Analytics workspace is used to collect and analyze Azure Monitor data from multiple subscriptions in one central location. Azure Activity Logs include information about which users or services performed actions in a subscription, and exporting those logs to a single Log Analytics workspace enables centralized monitoring across all subscriptions. Access reviews are for periodic access certification, Activity log filters only narrow what you view rather than centralizing collection, and Application Insights Profiler is for application performance diagnostics.

**Learn more:** [Azure Monitor activity log - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/platform/activity-log) · [Log Analytics workspace overview - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/log-analytics-workspace-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You create the following resources in an Azure subscription:  
  
- An Azure Container Registry instance named Registry1  
- An Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster named Cluster1  
  
You create a container image named App1 on your administrative workstation.  
  
You need to deploy App1 to Cluster1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Run the az acr build command.
Run the az aks create command.

questions.explanation:
AKS deploys container images by pulling them from a container registry such as Azure Container Registry. Because the AKS cluster and the ACR instance already exist and App1 was built on the local workstation, the first required step is to push that existing image into Registry1 so Cluster1 can pull it. Microsoft Learn states that to push an image to Azure Container Registry, you must first have an image, then tag and push it with standard Docker commands; AKS tutorials likewise describe building or otherwise preparing images and getting them into ACR before deploying them to the cluster.

**Learn more:** [Quickstart - Create Registry in Portal - Azure Container Registry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-get-started-portal) · [Introduction to Azure Container Registry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-intro)

questions.question:
You need to implement a backup solution for App1 after the application is moved.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation: To configure Azure Backup, the initial resource is a **Recovery Services vault**. The vault provides the backup management boundary for protected items, policies, and recovery points. A backup policy is created after the vault exists, Azure Backup Server is used for specific hybrid/on-premises backup scenarios rather than as the first step for standard Azure Backup, and a recovery plan is an Azure Site Recovery disaster recovery construct rather than a backup prerequisite.

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains the storage accounts shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783640477518-ldk1vg1b.png)  
  
You deploy a web app named App1 to the West US Azure region.  
  
You need to back up App1. The solution must minimize costs.  
  
Which storage account should you use as the backup target?
questions.explanation: For cost-minimized App Service backup, the storage account must be in the same region as the app to avoid cross-region data transfer costs. The image shows storage2 (BlobStorage) in West US and storage3 (BlockBlobStorage) also in West US. Storage2 is the standard, cost-effective choice for blob-based backup storage. While BlockBlobStorage provides specialization, standard BlobStorage is the lowest-cost option meeting the regional requirement.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains 10 virtual machines, a key vault named Vault1, and a network security group (NSG) named NSG1. All the resources are deployed to the **East US** Azure region.  
  
The virtual machines are protected by using NSG1. NSG1 is configured to block all outbound traffic to the internet.  
  
You need to ensure that the virtual machines can access Vault1. The solution must use the principle of least privilege and minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you configure as the **destination** of the outbound security rule for NSG1?
questions.explanation:
In an NSG rule, a **service tag** is the correct destination for allowing access from virtual machines to Azure Key Vault with least privilege and minimal administration. Service tags let NSG rules target Azure services such as **Key Vault** without hardcoding public IP ranges, and Microsoft maintains the underlying address prefixes automatically. An application security group is for grouping VM network interfaces, not Azure service endpoints, and using IP address ranges is not ideal because Key Vault service endpoint addresses are not intended to be managed as a fixed range by customers.

**Learn more:** [Network security groups and application security groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/networking/design-guide/network-application-security-groups) · [Azure service tags overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/service-tags-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing two peered virtual networks named VNet1 and VNet2. VNet1 has a VPN gateway that uses static routing.  
  
The on-premises network has a VPN connection that uses VNet1's VPN gateway.  
  
You need to configure access so that users on the on-premises network can connect to a virtual machine in VNet2. The solution must minimize costs.  
  
Which type of connectivity should you use?

options.text: Azure Firewall with a private IP address

questions.explanation:
Service chaining and user-defined routes (UDRs) enable traffic to be routed through a VPN gateway in a peered virtual network. This reuses VNet1’s existing VPN gateway to provide the required on-premises-to-VNet2 path, avoiding the additional cost of deploying ExpressRoute or application delivery and firewall services.

**Learn more:** [Azure Virtual Network Peering — Service chaining](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-peering-overview) · [Configure VPN gateway transit for virtual network peering](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/vpn-gateway-peering-gateway-transit)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains the virtual networks shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783640510875-0omq5xbw.png)  
  
You need to deploy an Azure firewall named AF1 to RG1 in the West US Azure region.  
  
To which virtual networks can AF1 be deployed?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Firewall instance must be created in a virtual network located in the same Azure region as the firewall. The virtual network does not have to be in the same resource group as the firewall resource, so a West US VNet in either RG1 or RG2 is valid. From the table, only VNET1 and VNET4 are in West US; VNET2 and VNET3 are in Central US and therefore can't host AF1. Microsoft Learn Azure Firewall deployment guidance states that the firewall is deployed in its own virtual network and that the related resources in the deployment must be in the same region.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Deploy and configure Azure Firewall and policy using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/tutorial-firewall-deploy-portal-policy) · [Deploy and configure Azure Firewall using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/tutorial-firewall-deploy-portal)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Standard-tier Azure App Service plan named Plan1.  
  
You need to ensure that Plan1 scales automatically when the web app’s CPU usage exceeds 80 percent.  
  
What should you select for Plan1?

options.text: Automatic in the Scale out method settings
Rules Based in the Scale out method settings
Premium P1 in the Scale up (App Service plan) settings
Standard S1 in the Scale up (App Service plan) settings
Manual in the Scale out method settings

questions.explanation:
Rules-based scale-out supports Azure autoscale rules that use metrics such as CPU percentage. The Standard tier supports autoscale; the Automatic scale-out method is traffic-based rather than CPU-threshold-based.

**Learn more:** [Automatic scaling in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/manage-automatic-scaling) · [Get started with autoscale in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/autoscale/autoscale-get-started?toc=%2Fazure%2Fapp-service%2Ftoc.json)
