You have an on-premises network.  
  
You have an Azure subscription that contains three virtual networks named VNET1, VNET2, and VNET3. The virtual networks are peered and connected to the on-premises network. The subscription contains the virtual machines shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783640511027-22jhs68p.png)  
  
You need to monitor connectivity between the virtual machines and the on-premises network by using Connection Monitor.  
  
What is the minimum number of connection monitors you should deploy?
questions.explanation:
Azure Connection Monitor is a region-specific Network Watcher resource, but each monitor can include multiple endpoints and test groups, including Azure VMs and on-premises machines. Because the virtual machines are located in two regions—West US and Central US—you need one connection monitor per source region to cover all VM-to-on-premises connectivity paths. That makes the minimum number of connection monitors 2.

**Learn more:** [Create a Connection Monitor - Azure Portal - Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/connection-monitor-create-using-portal) · [Connection Monitor Overview - Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/connection-monitor-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to make sure that **Group4** can be granted **Azure RBAC read-only** permissions for **all the Azure file shares**.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: On storage2, enable identity-based access for the file shares.
Recreate storage2 and set Hierarchical namespace to Enabled.
On storage1 and storage4, change the Account kind type to StorageV2 (general purpose v2).
Create a shared access signature (SAS) for storage1, storage2, and storage4.

questions.explanation: Azure file shares support read-only access through Azure RBAC when identity-based access is enabled for Azure Files on the storage account. This allows assigning built-in Azure Files data access roles to a Microsoft Entra group such as Group4. Enabling hierarchical namespace is unrelated to Azure Files RBAC, SAS tokens are a different authorization mechanism and do not grant Azure RBAC permissions, and merely changing an account to StorageV2 does not itself enable the required identity-based Azure Files authorization.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains two Log Analytics workspaces named Workspace1 and Workspace2 and 100 virtual machines that run Windows Server.  
  
You need to collect performance data and events from the virtual machines. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Logs must be sent to Workspace1 and Workspace2.  
- All Windows events must be captured.  
- All security events must be captured.  
  
What should you install and configure on each virtual machine?
questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor agent supports collecting Windows event logs and performance counters from Windows virtual machines by using data collection rules. Microsoft Learn also states that Windows event data and performance counter data can be sent to multiple Log Analytics workspaces, which meets the requirement to send the same data to Workspace1 and Workspace2. Security events are included by collecting the Security log through the Windows event data source. The Windows VM agent is only the guest agent used to manage extensions, and Azure Diagnostics extension is a legacy solution rather than the correct current monitoring agent for this requirement.

**Learn more:** [Collect Windows events from virtual machines with Azure Monitor Agent - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/vm/data-collection-windows-events) · [Collect performance counters from virtual machines with Azure Monitor - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/vm/data-collection-performance)

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Solution: enable **Floating IP**.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure internal load balancer used as the listener endpoint for a SQL Server Always On availability group on Azure virtual machines requires the load-balancing rule to have Floating IP enabled for direct server return. Microsoft Learn configuration guidance for availability group listeners includes enabling Floating IP on the load balancer rule, so this action satisfies the requirement.

**Learn more:** [Configure a Load Balancer & Availability Group Listener (Azure Portal) - SQL Server on Azure VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/virtual-machines/windows/availability-group-load-balancer-portal-configure?view=azuresql) · [Tutorial: Configure a SQL Server Always on Availability Group - SQL Server on Azure VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/virtual-machines/windows/availability-group-manually-configure-tutorial-single-subnet?view=azuresql)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Solution: You create an HTTP health probe on port 1433.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure internal load balancer for a SQL Server Always On availability group listener must use a load-balancer health probe configuration supported by the Windows Server Failover Cluster and listener setup. Microsoft guidance for SQL Server availability group listeners on Azure virtual machines uses a **TCP** health probe on a dedicated probe port, with corresponding cluster parameters configured for the listener. An **HTTP** probe on port **1433** is not the required listener probe configuration, so it does not satisfy the goal.

**Learn more:** [Configure a load balancer for an availability group on Azure SQL Server VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/virtual-machines/windows/availability-group-load-balancer-portal-configure) · [Tutorial: Configure an availability group listener across multiple subnets with an Azure Load Balancer](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/database-engine/availability-groups/windows/tutorial-configure-listener-azure-portal?view=sql-server-ver16)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Solution: You configure **Session persistence** to **Client IP**.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
For an Azure internal load balancer used as a SQL Server Always On availability group listener, Microsoft Learn specifies the listener load-balancing rule with **Session Persistence = None** and **Floating IP (direct server return) = Enabled**. Because the required setting is **None**, configuring **Client IP** does not satisfy the listener configuration requirement.

**Learn more:** [Configure a Load Balancer & Availability Group Listener (Azure Portal) - SQL Server on Azure VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/virtual-machines/windows/availability-group-load-balancer-portal-configure?view=azuresql) · [Tutorial: Configure a SQL Server Always on Availability Group - SQL Server on Azure VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/virtual-machines/windows/availability-group-manually-configure-tutorial-single-subnet?view=azuresql)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to deploy an Azure virtual machine scale set that contains five instances as quickly as possible.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Deploy five virtual machines. Modify the Availability Zones settings for each virtual machine.
Deploy five virtual machines. Modify the Size setting for each virtual machine.
Deploy one virtual machine scale set that is set to VM (virtual machines) orchestration mode.
Deploy one virtual machine scale set that is set to ScaleSetVM orchestration mode.

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets are designed to create and manage multiple identical VM instances as a single resource. For the fastest deployment of five like-for-like instances, the uniform scale set model is the best fit because the instances are managed as scale-set VMs rather than as individually managed Azure virtual machines. Azure documentation distinguishes Flexible orchestration, which supports standard Azure VM instances and greater per-VM flexibility, from Uniform orchestration, which uses scale-set VM instances for large-scale identical workloads and simpler rapid provisioning.

**Learn more:** [Orchestration modes for Virtual Machine Scale Sets in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machine-scale-sets/virtual-machine-scale-sets-orchestration-modes) · [Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machine-scale-sets/overview)

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.explanation:
For Ubuntu and other Linux VMs in Azure, custom deployment tasks such as adding a trusted root CA are typically done at provisioning time by passing cloud-init or other custom data. Microsoft Learn documents using `az vm create` with `--custom-data` for this purpose when creating Linux VMs. `New-AzureRmVm` belongs to the retired AzureRM module, and `Create-AzVM` is not the standard VM creation cmdlet.

**Learn more:** [Custom data and cloud-init on Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/custom-data) · [Overview of cloud-init support for Linux VMs in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/linux/using-cloud-init)

You have a public load balancer that distributes ports 80 and 443 across three virtual machines named VM1, VM2, and VM3.  
  
You need to send all Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) connections to VM3 only.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: a new public load balancer for VM3

questions.explanation:
An inbound NAT rule is the Azure Load Balancer feature used to forward traffic from a frontend IP and port to one specific backend virtual machine. That is the correct configuration for directing RDP traffic to VM3 only, whereas a load-balancing rule would distribute traffic across multiple backend VMs instead of targeting a single VM. Microsoft Learn identifies inbound NAT rules as the mechanism for port forwarding to a designated virtual machine and specifically notes RDP as a typical scenario.

**Learn more:** [Inbound NAT rules - Azure Load Balancer | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/inbound-nat-rules) · [Azure Load Balancer portal settings | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/manage)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains an Azure virtual machine named VM1. VM1 runs a financial reporting app named App1 that does not support multiple active instances.  
  
At the end of each month, CPU usage for VM1 peaks when App1 runs.  
  
You need to create a scheduled runbook to increase the processor performance of VM1 at the end of each month.  
  
What task should you include in the runbook?

options.text: Add the Azure Performance Diagnostics agent to VM1.
Modify the VM size property of VM1.
Add VM1 to a scale set.
Increase the vCPU quota for the subscription.
Add a Desired State Configuration (DSC) extension to VM1.

questions.explanation:
To increase CPU performance for a single Azure VM, you resize the VM to a larger size/SKU by changing its VM size property. That scales the existing VM up rather than out, which fits an application that cannot run on multiple active instances. Azure documentation for resizing virtual machines states that you can scale a VM up or down by changing its size, and Azure CLI exposes this directly through `az vm resize`.

**Learn more:** [Resize a virtual machine - Azure Virtual Machines | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/sizes/resize-vm) · [az vm resize - Azure CLI | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/vm?view=azure-cli-latest#az-vm-resize)

You have an Azure subscription named Subscription1.  
  
You have 5 TB of data that you need to transfer to Subscription1.  
  
You plan to use an Azure Import/Export job.  
  
What can you use as the destination for the imported data?
questions.explanation:
Azure Import/Export supports importing data by shipping drives to an Azure datacenter, and the supported import targets are Azure Blob storage and Azure Files. Of the available choices, only Azure Blob storage is a supported destination for imported data.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Import/Export documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/import-export/) · [Using Azure Import/Export to transfer data to and from Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/import-export/storage-import-export-service)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription named Subscription1.  
  
You have 5 TB of data that you need to transfer to Subscription1.  
  
You plan to use an Azure Import/Export job.  
  
What can you use as the destination for the imported data?
questions.explanation:
Azure Import/Export supports importing data by shipping drives to Azure for copying into Azure Storage. The supported import destinations are Azure Blob Storage and Azure Files. Of the available options, only Azure Blob Storage is supported, so it is the correct destination.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Import/Export documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/import-export/) · [Using Azure Import/Export to transfer data to and from Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/import-export/storage-import-export-service)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription.  
  
In the Azure portal, you plan to create a storage account named `storage1` with the following settings:  
  
- **Performance:** Standard  
- **Replication:** Zone-redundant storage (ZRS)  
- **Access tier (default):** Cool  
- **Hierarchical namespace:** Disabled  
  
You need to make sure that you can set **Account kind** for `storage1` to **BlockBlobStorage**.  
  
Which setting should you change first?
questions.explanation:
A BlockBlobStorage account is a premium block blob storage account type, so it requires **Premium** performance. With **Standard** performance selected, the BlockBlobStorage account kind is not available. ZRS can be supported for premium block blob accounts, while the listed hierarchical namespace setting does not prevent choosing that account kind. The access tier shown as Cool is also incompatible with premium block blob accounts, but the prerequisite that enables the BlockBlobStorage account kind in the portal is changing the performance tier to Premium.

**Learn more:** [Storage Account Overview - Azure Storage | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-sg/azure/storage/common/storage-account-overview) · [Premium block blob storage accounts - Azure Storage | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-blob-block-blob-premium)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant called contoso.com.  
  
You collaborate with an external partner called fabrikam.com.  
  
You plan to invite fabrikam.com users to the contoso.com tenant.  
  
You need to ensure that invitations can be sent only to fabrikam.com users.  
  
What should you configure in the Microsoft Entra admin center?

options.text: From Cross-tenant access settings, configure the Tenant restrictions settings.
From Cross-tenant access settings, configure the Microsoft cloud settings.
From External collaboration settings, configure the Guest user access restrictions settings.
From External collaboration settings, configure the Collaboration restrictions settings.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra External collaboration settings include Collaboration restrictions, which can use an allowlist to permit B2B invitations only to specified email domains. Adding `fabrikam.com` as the allowed domain prevents invitations to users from all other domains.

**Learn more:** [Allow or block B2B collaboration with organizations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/allow-deny-list) · [Configure external collaboration settings for B2B in Microsoft Entra External ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/external-collaboration-settings-configure)

questions.question:
You plan to back up an Azure virtual machine named VM1.  
  
You discover that the **Backup Pre-Check** status shows **Warning**.  
  
What is one possible cause of the **Warning** status?

options.text: VM1 does not have the latest version of the Azure VM Agent (WaAppAgent.exe) installed.
A Recovery Services vault is unavailable.

questions.explanation: A Backup Pre-Check **Warning** for an Azure virtual machine can occur when the Azure VM Agent is missing or not updated to a current version. Azure Backup uses the VM agent for extension-based coordination and application-consistent backup behavior; if the agent is outdated, backup may still be possible, but it can raise a warning because recommended backup functionality may not be fully available.

You create a public Azure DNS zone named adatum.com and a private Azure DNS zone named contoso.com.  
  
For contoso.com, you create a virtual network link named link1 as shown in the exhibit. (Click the Exhibit tab.)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783632865773-ung9va72.jpg)  
  
You discover that VM1 can resolve names in contoso.com but cannot resolve names in adatum.com. VM1 can resolve other hosts on the Internet.  
  
You need to ensure that VM1 can resolve host names in adatum.com.

options.text: Update the DNS suffix on VM1 to be adatum.com
Configure the name servers for adatum.com at the domain registrar
Create an SRV record in the contoso.com zone
Modify the Access control (IAM) settings for link1

questions.explanation:
A public Azure DNS zone answers queries for its domain only after the domain is delegated to Azure DNS by updating the domain registrar with the Azure-assigned name servers. The private zone link for contoso.com correctly enables resolution from VNET1 only for that private namespace. Changing the VM DNS suffix, adding an SRV record in a different zone, or modifying IAM on the virtual network link would not make names in the public adatum.com zone resolvable.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have five Azure virtual machines running Windows Server 2016, and those virtual machines are configured as web servers.  
  
You also have an Azure load balancer named **LB1** that provides load-balancing services for the virtual machines.  
  
You need to make sure that visitors are served by the same web server for each request.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: Floating IP (direct server return) to Enabled

questions.explanation:
Azure Load Balancer achieves client-to-server stickiness by using **session persistence**. Setting **Session persistence** to **Client IP** uses source IP affinity so successive requests from the same client IP address are sent to the same backend virtual machine. The other settings do not provide this behavior: Floating IP is for direct server return scenarios, Protocol controls transport type, and Idle Time-out only changes how long inactive flows are kept.

**Learn more:** [Azure Load Balancer distribution modes | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/distribution-mode-concepts) · [Configure Azure Load Balancer distribution mode | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/load-balancer-distribution-mode)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You plan to bulk import users.  
  
You need to ensure that imported user objects are automatically added as members of a specific group according to each user's department. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create groups that use the Assigned membership type.
Create an Azure Resource Manager (ARM) template.
Create groups that use the Dynamic User membership type.
Write a PowerShell script that parses an import file.
Create an XML file that contains user information and the appropriate attributes.
Create a CSV file that contains user information and the appropriate attributes.

questions.explanation:
Dynamic User membership groups automatically evaluate membership rules using user attributes, including rules such as `user.department -eq "Sales"`. Bulk user creation uses a CSV template that includes the `Department [department]` attribute. Supplying each imported user's department in that CSV enables the dynamic group rule to add the applicable users automatically.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have five Azure virtual machines that run Windows Server 2016. The virtual machines are configured as web servers.  
  
You have an Azure load balancer named LB1 that provides load-balancing services for the virtual machines.  
  
You need to ensure that visitors are served by the same web server for each request.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: Floating IP (direct server return) to Disabled
Floating IP (direct server return) to Enabled

questions.explanation:
Azure Load Balancer provides stickiness by using **session persistence** on the load-balancing rule. Setting session persistence to **Client IP** enables source IP affinity, which causes successive requests from the same client IP address to be sent to the same backend virtual machine. Floating IP (direct server return) does not control session affinity.

VNET1 is linked to a private DNS zone named contoso.com that contains the records shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783637476009-tyo44g0d.png)  
  
You need to ping VM2 from VM1.  
  
Which DNS names can you use to ping VM2?
questions.explanation:
Only an address record that supports forward name resolution to 10.0.0.5 can be used to reach VM2 by name. In Azure Private DNS, an **A** record maps a name to an IPv4 address, so **comp2.contoso.com** resolves to VM2. A **TXT** record does not provide an IP address, a **CNAME** is usable only if it ultimately points to a resolvable address record, and a **PTR** record is for reverse lookups rather than resolving a host name to an IP address. Because **comp3** points to **comp1**, which is a TXT record, and **comp4** is PTR-only, neither can be used to ping VM2.

**Learn more:** [Azure Private DNS Zone Overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/private-dns-privatednszone) · [Private DNS records overview - Azure Private DNS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/dns-private-records)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have five Azure virtual machines that run Windows Server 2016. The virtual machines are configured as web servers.  
  
You have an Azure load balancer named LB1 that provides load-balancing services for the virtual machines.  
  
You need to ensure that visitors are served by the same web server for each request.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: Floating IP (direct server return) to Disabled

questions.explanation:
Azure Load Balancer must be configured for session affinity to keep a client on the same backend instance. Setting **Session persistence** to **Client IP** uses source IP affinity so successive requests from the same client IP address are routed to the same virtual machine. A health probe only checks backend availability, Idle Time-out controls how long idle flows are kept, and Floating IP is unrelated to client affinity. This behavior is documented in Microsoft Learn for Azure Load Balancer distribution modes and configuration.

**Learn more:** [Azure Load Balancer distribution modes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/distribution-mode-concepts) · [Configure Azure Load Balancer distribution mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/load-balancer-distribution-mode)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Solution: You change the Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) authentication policies.

questions.explanation:
A point-to-site VPN configured to use a self-signed certificate relies on certificate authentication, so each client computer must have a valid client certificate installed. Microsoft Learn states that when you want to install a client certificate on another client computer, you must export it as a .pfx and install it there. Modifying Azure AD authentication policies does not enable Computer2 to authenticate to a certificate-based P2S connection.

**Learn more:** [Configure VPN gateway for P2S certificate authentication: Azure portal - Azure VPN Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/point-to-site-certificate-gateway) · [Install a Point-to-Site client certificate - Azure VPN Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/point-to-site-how-to-vpn-client-install-azure-cert)

Solution: You join Computer2 to Azure Active Directory (Azure AD).  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation: A certificate-authenticated Azure point-to-site VPN requires the connecting device to have a valid client certificate, chained to a root certificate uploaded to the Azure VPN gateway. Azure AD join does not satisfy certificate-based point-to-site authentication and does not provide the needed self-signed client certificate for Computer2. To connect successfully from Computer2, the appropriate client certificate and private key must be installed on that computer.

questions.explanation:
For Azure point-to-site VPNs that use self-signed certificate authentication, every client computer must have a valid client certificate installed locally. Microsoft Learn states that if you want to use the certificate on another client computer, you can export the client certificate from the original computer as a .pfx file, including the certificate chain, and install it on the other computer. That enables Computer2 to authenticate to the P2S VPN.

**Learn more:** [Install a Point-to-Site client certificate - Azure VPN Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/point-to-site-how-to-vpn-client-install-azure-cert) · [Configure VPN gateway for P2S certificate authentication: Azure portal - Azure VPN Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/point-to-site-certificate-gateway)

Setting the IPSec Policy Agent service to start automatically does not provide the required certificate-based authentication and is not the required step to enable Computer2 to connect. The needed action is to make the appropriate client certificate available on Computer2.

The other properties—`kind`, `sku`, and `location`—are storage account resource configuration options, not deployment-targeting settings.

questions.question:
You administer a solution in Azure that is currently experiencing performance issues.  
  
You need to identify the cause of the performance issues related to metrics on the Azure infrastructure.  
  
Which of the following tools should you use?
questions.explanation: Azure Monitor is the correct tool because it collects and analyzes Azure metrics and logs for infrastructure resources, allowing you to investigate performance issues by reviewing platform metrics, alerts, and diagnostic data. Azure Activity Log shows control-plane events, Azure Advisor provides optimization recommendations, and Azure Traffic Analytics is limited to network traffic analysis rather than broad Azure infrastructure performance metrics.

questions.question:
Solution: You assign the Network Contributor role at the subscription level to Admin1.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft's documented Network Watcher RBAC permissions explicitly state that the built-in Network Contributor role does not include the Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces/*, Microsoft.Insights/dataCollectionRules/*, or Microsoft.Insights/dataCollectionEndpoints/* actions that Traffic Analytics requires. Because Traffic Analytics writes to and reads from a Log Analytics workspace in addition to Network Watcher resources, assigning only Network Contributor at the subscription scope is insufficient, so the solution does not meet the goal.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure RBAC Permissions - Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/required-rbac-permissions)

Solution: You assign the Network Contributor role at the subscription level to Admin1.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Assigning the **Owner** role at the **subscription** scope gives Admin1 full management rights over resources in that subscription. For Azure Network Watcher Traffic Analytics, Microsoft states that enabling the feature requires permissions available through built-in roles such as **Owner**, **Contributor**, or **Network Contributor** at the appropriate scope. Therefore, assigning **Owner** at the subscription level is sufficient to enable Traffic Analytics.

**Learn more:** [Azure RBAC Permissions - Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/required-rbac-permissions) · [What role is required to be enabled at Subscription scope to enable Traffic Analytics for an Azure subscription. - Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/1330227/what-role-is-required-to-be-enabled-at-subscriptio)

To enable or disable Traffic Analytics, the user needs broader permissions such as Owner, Contributor, or Network Contributor, or a custom role that includes the required Network Watcher-related actions.\

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure web app named **webapp1**.  
  
Users report that they frequently encounter **HTTP 500** errors when connecting to **webapp1**.  
  
You need to give the developers of **webapp1** real-time access to the connection errors. The solution must include **all connection error details**.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From webapp1, enable Web server logging
From Azure Monitor, create a workbook
From Azure Monitor, create a Service Health alert
From webapp1, turn on Application Logging

questions.explanation:
Web server logging captures raw HTTP request data in the W3C extended log format, including client IP, HTTP method, resource URI, and response code, and can be watched live through the Log Stream pane, giving developers real-time visibility into every connection-level detail behind the HTTP 500 responses. Application Logging instead records only what the application code explicitly chooses to log, so it cannot guarantee that all connection error details are captured. A workbook or a Service Health alert does not provide this raw request-level diagnostic data at all.

**Learn more:** [Enable Diagnostic Logging - Azure App Service | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/troubleshoot-diagnostic-logs)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have the Azure virtual networks shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783646931691-epbd4t7k.png)  
  
Which virtual networks can be peered with VNet1?
questions.explanation:
Azure virtual network peering is allowed only when the two VNets have **non-overlapping IP address spaces**. VNet2 cannot be peered with VNet1 because `10.11.0.0/17` overlaps with VNet1's `10.11.0.0/16`. VNet3 (`10.10.0.0/22`) and VNet4 (`192.168.16.0/22`) do not overlap with VNet1, so both are eligible. Their being in different Azure regions does not block peering, because Azure supports peering VNets in the same region or different regions.

**Learn more:** [Create, Change, or Delete Azure Virtual Network Peering | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-manage-peering) · [Troubleshoot virtual network peering issues - Azure | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-troubleshoot-peering-issues)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Solution: You add an inbound security rule to **NSG-Subnet1** that allows connections from the **Any** source to the `*` destination on port range **3389** by using the **TCP** protocol. You remove **NSG-VM1** from the network interface of **VM1**.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Remote Desktop access to an Azure VM from the internet requires inbound **TCP 3389** to be allowed. When an NSG is associated to both a subnet and a NIC, inbound traffic must be permitted by both; if the NIC NSG is removed, only the subnet NSG is evaluated for that path. Adding a subnet-level allow rule for TCP 3389 and removing the NIC-level NSG eliminates the existing NIC rule set that allowed only UDP 3389, so the VM can receive RDP traffic from the internet.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot NSG misconfigurations that block traffic in Azure Virtual Network - Azure | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-troubleshoot-nsg-blocking-traffic) · [How Network Security Groups Filter Network Traffic in Azure | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/network-security-group-how-it-works)

questions.question:
Solution: You add an inbound security rule to **NSG-Subnet1** that allows connections from the **Internet** source to the **VirtualNetwork** destination on port range **3389** and uses the **UDP** protocol.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation: Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) uses TCP port 3389 by default, not UDP. Although the proposed rule correctly targets port 3389 and the Internet-to-VirtualNetwork path, it specifies the UDP protocol instead of TCP. Since UDP 3389 is not the standard RDP protocol, the connection will not succeed. Additionally, NSG rules are evaluated by the 5-tuple (source, source port, destination, destination port, protocol), so UDP and TCP are completely distinct rules.

questions.question:
Solution: You add an inbound security rule to **NSG-Subnet1** and **NSG-VM1** that allows connections from the **Internet** source to the **VirtualNetwork** destination for port range **3389** and uses the **TCP** protocol.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation: Adding inbound security rules to both NSG-Subnet1 and NSG-VM1 that allow Internet source to VirtualNetwork destination on TCP port 3389 satisfies the RDP connectivity requirement. Azure evaluates inbound traffic against the subnet NSG first, then the network interface NSG—both must allow the traffic. Since the existing custom rule allows UDP 3389 and the new rule adds TCP 3389, the TCP-based RDP protocol will be permitted through both NSG layers.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to migrate **50 virtual machines** from **VMware vSphere** to the subscription.  
  
You create a **Recovery Services vault**.  
  
What should you do next?

options.text: Deploy an Open Virtualization Application (OVA) template to vSphere.

questions.explanation:
For VMware vSphere machines that will be moved to Azure by using Azure Site Recovery, the next required step after creating the Recovery Services vault is to deploy the Site Recovery configuration server or replication appliance in the VMware environment from the provided OVA/OVF template. That appliance registers with the vault, discovers the vSphere environment, and enables replication setup. Recovery plans are created after protection is configured, and an extended network is not part of the required initial workflow. Microsoft Learn documents this VMware setup as downloading and deploying the OVA template for the configuration server/appliance from the vault workflow.

**Learn more:** [Deploy the configuration server in Azure Site Recovery - Azure Site Recovery | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/site-recovery/vmware-azure-deploy-configuration-server) · [Set up Azure Site Recovery for Azure VMware Solution VMs - Azure Site Recovery | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/site-recovery/avs-tutorial-replication)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Subscription1 that contains an Azure virtual machine named VM1. VM1 is in a resource group named RG1.  
  
VM1 runs services that will be used to deploy resources to RG1.  
  
You need to ensure that a service running on VM1 can manage the resources in RG1 by using the identity of VM1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From the Azure portal, modify the Managed Identity settings of VM1
From the Azure portal, modify the Access control (IAM) settings of RG1
From the Azure portal, modify the Access control (IAM) settings of VM1
From the Azure portal, modify the Policies settings of RG1

questions.explanation:
A virtual machine must have a system-assigned or user-assigned managed identity enabled before that identity can be granted Azure RBAC access to a resource group. Microsoft Learn states that after you enable a system-assigned managed identity on a VM, you can then grant it a role on the target scope such as a resource group. Because the requirement is to use the identity of VM1 itself, the first step is enabling or modifying the managed identity settings on VM1; assigning IAM on RG1 comes afterward.

**Learn more:** [Configure managed identities on Azure virtual machines (VMs) - Managed identities for Azure resources](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/how-to-configure-managed-identities) · [Use Azure portal to grant a managed identity access to a resource - Managed identities for Azure resources](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/grant-managed-identity-resource-access-azure-portal)

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.explanation:
Azure Availability Zones for virtual machines require zonal deployment to be selected in the VM's availability settings, and Azure managed disks are the disk model that supports Availability Zones. Unmanaged disks are not supported for this scenario, so the VM must be changed to use managed disks, and the availability setting must be changed from no redundancy to an Availability Zone option. The existing image, size, and Standard HDD OS disk type do not by themselves block zonal creation in this configuration.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Disk Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/managed-disks-overview) · [Unmanaged disks have been retired - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/unmanaged-disks-deprecation)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Subscription1 and an on-premises deployment of Microsoft System Center Service Manager.  
  
Subscription1 contains a virtual machine named VM1.  
  
You need to make sure that an alert is created in Service Manager when the available memory on VM1 falls below 10 percent.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Deploy the IT Service Management Connector (ITSM)

questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor sends alerts to ITSM systems through the IT Service Management Connector (ITSMC). Microsoft Learn states that before you can create ITSM work items from Azure alerts, you must first install or deploy ITSMC and then create the connection to the ITSM product. Because the requirement is to have a Service Manager alert/work item generated from an Azure VM memory condition, the prerequisite first step is deploying the IT Service Management Connector.

**Learn more:** [Connect Azure to ITSM tools by using IT Service Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/itsmc-definition) · [Connect ServiceNow with IT Service Management Connector - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/itsmc-connections-servicenow)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure virtual network named VNet1 that includes a subnet named Subnet1. Subnet1 contains three Azure virtual machines, and each virtual machine has a public IP address.  
  
The virtual machines host several applications that are available to users on the Internet over port 443.  
  
Your on-premises network has a site-to-site VPN connection to VNet1.  
  
You discover that the virtual machines are accessible by using Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) from both the Internet and the on-premises network.  
  
You need to prevent RDP access to the virtual machines from the Internet, unless the RDP connection is established from the on-premises network. The solution must ensure that all the applications remain accessible to Internet users.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Modify the address space of the local network gateway
Create a deny rule in a network security group (NSG) that is linked to Subnet1
Remove the public IP addresses from the virtual machines
Modify the address space of Subnet1

questions.explanation:
A network security group linked to Subnet1 can filter inbound traffic by protocol, port, and source. Creating a deny inbound rule for TCP port 3389 from Internet sources blocks direct RDP from the public Internet, while higher-priority allow rules can permit RDP from the on-premises address range across the site-to-site VPN. NSGs can also continue to allow HTTPS traffic on port 443, so the Internet-facing applications remain reachable. Azure NSG rules are designed for exactly this kind of subnet-level access control.

**Learn more:** [Azure network security groups overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/network-security-groups-overview) · [Tutorial: Filter network traffic with a network security group using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-network/tutorial-filter-network-traffic)

Your company has an Azure subscription named **Subscription1**.  
  
The company also has two on-premises servers named **Server1** and **Server2** that run **Windows Server 2016**. **Server1** is configured as a DNS server that has a primary DNS zone named **adatum.com**. **adatum.com** contains **1,000 DNS records**.  
  
You manage **Server1** and **Subscription1** from **Server2**. **Server2** has the following tools installed:  
  
- The **DNS Manager** console  
- **Azure PowerShell**  
- **Azure CLI 2.0**  
  
You need to move the **adatum.com** zone to an Azure DNS zone in **Subscription1**. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure DNS supports importing an existing DNS zone file directly by using Azure CLI with `az network dns zone import`. For a Windows DNS-hosted zone, the zone file can be obtained from the Windows DNS server, and importing that file creates the Azure DNS zone and bulk-loads the records, which is the least administrative work for a zone with 1,000 records. DNS Manager is for administering Windows DNS, not migrating the zone into Azure DNS, and Azure PowerShell is not the documented bulk-import path used for this scenario.

**Learn more:** [Import and export a domain zone file - Azure CLI - Azure DNS | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/dns-import-export) · [az network dns zone | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/network/dns/zone?view=azure-cli-latest)

You have an Azure subscription. The subscription contains virtual machines that run Windows Server.  
  
You have a data collection rule (DCR) named Rule1.  
  
You plan to use the Azure Monitor Agent to collect events from Windows **System** event logs.  
  
You only need to collect system events that have an ID of **1001**.  
  
Which type of query should you use for the data source in Rule1?
questions.explanation:
For Azure Monitor Agent, a DCR Windows Event Logs data source filters collected Windows events by using **XPath** queries. Microsoft Learn specifies that custom Windows event filtering in a DCR uses entries in the form `LogName!XPathQuery`, and it gives examples such as filtering the System log by `EventID`. Therefore, to collect only System events with ID 1001, the required query type is XPath.

**Learn more:** [Collect Windows events from virtual machines with Azure Monitor Agent - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/vm/data-collection-windows-events) · [az monitor data-collection rule windows-event-log | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/monitor/data-collection/rule/windows-event-log?view=azure-cli-latest)

You have an existing Azure subscription that contains 10 virtual machines.  
  
You need to monitor the latency between your on-premises network and the virtual machines.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation: Network Performance Monitor (part of Azure Monitor/Network Watcher) is specifically designed to monitor latency and network performance metrics across hybrid environments, including paths from on-premises networks to Azure virtual machines over time. Service Map visualizes application dependencies, Connection troubleshoot performs point-in-time diagnostics, and Effective routes displays routing configuration—none of which provide the continuous latency monitoring required for this hybrid scenario.

questions.explanation:
To upload the contents of a local directory to Azure Blob Storage, AzCopy uses the `azcopy copy` command with the local folder as the source, the container URL as the destination, and `--recursive` to include all files and subfolders. Microsoft Learn documents `azcopy copy '<local-directory-path>' 'https://<storage-account-name>.blob.core.windows.net/<container-name>' --recursive` for uploading an entire directory. By contrast, `az storage blob copy start` and `start-batch` are blob-to-blob copy operations, not local-folder uploads. ([learn.microsoft.com](https://learn.microsoft.com/da-dk/azure/storage/common/storage-use-azcopy-blobs-upload?utm_source=openai))

**Learn more:** [Upload files to Azure Blob storage by using AzCopy v10](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-use-azcopy-blobs-upload) · [az storage blob copy | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/storage/blob/copy?view=azure-cli-latest)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains a Recovery Services vault named Vault1.  
  
You need to enable multi-user authorization (MAU) for Vault1.  
  
Which resource should you create first?
questions.explanation:
Multi-user authorization for Azure Backup on a Recovery Services vault is provided through **Resource Guard**. The setup flow is to create a Resource Guard first, assign the required access such as Reader on it to the backup admin as needed, and then enable MAU on the vault by linking the vault to that Resource Guard. Administrative units, managed identities, and custom Azure roles are not the prerequisite resource that enables MAU for a Recovery Services vault.

**Learn more:** [Configure Multi-user authorization using Resource Guard - Azure Backup | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/multi-user-authorization) · [Tutorial - Enable Multi-user authorization using Resource Guard - Azure Backup | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/multi-user-authorization-tutorial)

You need to recommend a solution to automate the configuration for the finance department users. The solution must satisfy the technical requirements.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: dynamic groups and conditional access policies
an Azure logic app and the Microsoft Identity Management (MIM) client

questions.explanation: Dynamic groups can automatically assign users to a group based on attributes such as their department, which lets finance users be targeted automatically as membership changes. Conditional Access policies can then be assigned to that group so the required configuration is enforced without manual updates. Azure AD B2C is intended for external identities, Azure AD Identity Protection focuses on risk-based detection and remediation, and MIM with a Logic App is not the native choice for attribute-driven user targeting in Azure AD.

questions.explanation:
For Azure App Service to import and use a certificate from Azure Key Vault, the vault must grant the App Service resource provider/service principal data-plane permission to read the certificate and its secret. This is done by creating a Key Vault access policy for the Microsoft Azure App Service principal. A managed identity on the web app is for application access to Key Vault from code, not for App Service platform certificate import and binding.

You are planning the migration of App1 to Azure.  
  
You create a network security group (NSG).  
  
You need to recommend a solution that provides users with access to App1.  
  
What should you recommend?

options.text: Create an incoming security rule for port 443 from the Internet. Associate the NSG to the subnet that contains the web servers.
Create an outgoing security rule for port 443 from the Internet. Associate the NSG to the subnet that contains the web servers.
Create an incoming security rule for port 443 from the Internet. Associate the NSG to all the subnets.
Create an outgoing security rule for port 443 from the Internet. Associate the NSG to all the subnets.

questions.explanation: To allow users to reach App1 over HTTPS, the network security group must permit **inbound** traffic from the Internet on TCP port 443 to the subnet or NIC hosting the web servers. An outbound rule would not enable external users to initiate connections to the application, and applying the NSG to all subnets is broader than required for exposing only the web tier.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named `contoso.onmicrosoft.com` that contains 100 user accounts.  
  
You purchase 10 Azure AD Premium P2 licenses for the tenant.  
  
You need to ensure that 10 users can use all the Azure AD Premium features.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Licenses blade of Azure AD, assign a license
From the Groups blade of each user, invite the users to a group
From the Azure AD domain, add an enterprise application
From the Directory role blade of each user, modify the directory role

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID Premium P2 capabilities are licensed per user, so the required users must be assigned those purchased licenses. Simply placing users in a group, adding an enterprise application, or changing directory roles does not grant entitlement to Premium P2 features. The correct action is to assign the Azure AD Premium P2 licenses to the 10 users.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra users, groups, licenses, and domains documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/) · [Assign Microsoft 365 licenses to user accounts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/enterprise/assign-licenses-to-user-accounts?view=o365-worldwide)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to satisfy the technical requirements for the KEK.  
  
Which PowerShell cmdlet and key should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Disk Encryption is enabled on an IaaS virtual machine by using `Set-AzVMDiskEncryptionExtension`, which accepts a key encryption key to wrap the disk encryption key. Azure Disk Encryption requires an RSA key for the KEK and does not support elliptic-curve keys; therefore, the RSA 4096-bit Key1 is suitable.

**Learn more:** [Set-AzVMDiskEncryptionExtension (Az.Compute)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.compute/set-azvmdiskencryptionextension?view=azps-16.0.0) · [Creating and configuring a key vault for Azure Disk Encryption on a Windows VM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/disk-encryption-key-vault)

questions.question:
You need to configure WebApp1 to meet the technical requirements.  
  
Which certificate can you use from Vault1?
questions.explanation:
App Service imports a certificate from Key Vault as a PFX (PKCS#12) package containing the certificate and its private key, so only the PKCS#12 certificates — Cert1 and Cert2 — can be used directly. A PEM-encoded certificate must first be converted to PFX before it can be imported.\
\
**Learn more:** [Add a TLS/SSL certificate in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-ssl-certificate?tabs=apex%2CRBAC#import-a-certificate-from-key-vault)

questions.question:
You need to implement the planned changes for the storage account content.  
  
Which containers and file shares can you use to organize the content?
questions.explanation:
Organizing content into a directory structure inside a blob container requires a hierarchical namespace, which only storage1's cont1 has — cont2 is in the account without it and only simulates folders through name prefixes. Azure Files shares are directory-based by nature, so share1 and share2 can both be used regardless of the namespace setting.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Data Lake Storage hierarchical namespace](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/data-lake-storage-namespace)

questions.question:
You need to configure encryption for the virtual machines. The solution must satisfy the technical requirements.  
  
Which virtual machines can be encrypted?
questions.explanation:
Azure Disk Encryption supports the Windows VM with a basic volume and the RHEL VM with standard SSDs. It does not support ephemeral OS disks, dynamic volumes, or Windows VMs that use Write Accelerator disks. Therefore, VM2 and VM3 are eligible for encryption.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Disk Encryption scenarios on Windows VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/disk-encryption-windows) · [Azure Disk Encryption scenarios on Linux VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/linux/disk-encryption-linux)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription named Subscription1 that contains an Azure Log Analytics workspace named Workspace1.  
  
You need to view the error events from a table named Event.  
  
Which query should you run in Workspace1?
questions.explanation: Azure Log Analytics uses Kusto Query Language (KQL), not SQL or PowerShell. In KQL, the `search in (Event) \"error\"` statement searches the `Event` table for records containing the term `error`. The other options use invalid syntax for Log Analytics: `is` is not the correct equality operator in this context, `select *` is SQL syntax, and `Get-Event` is a PowerShell cmdlet rather than a workspace query.

You create an App Service plan named Plan1 and an Azure web app named webapp1.  
  
You discover that the option to create a staging slot is unavailable.  
  
You need to create a staging slot for Plan1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From Plan1, scale up the App Service plan
From webapp1, modify the Application settings
From webapp1, add a custom domain
From Plan1, scale out the App Service plan

questions.explanation:
Deployment slots are a feature of the App Service plan pricing tier, not a web app setting. Azure App Service supports staging/deployment slots only in the Standard, Premium, or Isolated tiers, so if the slot option is unavailable, the plan must first be scaled up to a tier that includes that feature.

**Learn more:** [Set up staging environments in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/deploy-staging-slots) · [Azure App Service plans](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-hosting-plans)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Subscription1 that contains a virtual network named VNet1. VNet1 is in a resource group named RG1.  
  
Subscription1 has a user named User1. User1 has the following roles:  
  
- Reader  
- Security Admin  
- Security Reader  
  
You need to make sure that User1 can assign the Reader role for VNet1 to other users.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Remove User1 from the Security Reader role for Subscription1. Assign User1 the Contributor role for RG1.
Assign User1 the User Access Administrator role for VNet1.
Remove User1 from the Security Reader and Reader roles for Subscription1.
Assign User1 the Contributor role for VNet1.

questions.explanation:
Assigning Azure RBAC roles requires permission to manage access at the target scope. The **User Access Administrator** built-in role allows management of user access to Azure resources, including creating role assignments, while **Contributor** can manage resources but cannot grant RBAC access. **Reader**, **Security Admin**, and **Security Reader** do not provide permission to assign the Reader role on a virtual network. Scoping **User Access Administrator** to **VNet1** gives the required least-privilege access for that resource.

**Learn more:** [Azure built-in roles - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles) · [Understand Azure role assignments - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/role-assignments)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains the storage accounts shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783632932216-o7ox209s.png)  
  
You plan to manage the data stored in the accounts by using lifecycle management rules.  
  
To which storage accounts can you apply lifecycle management rules?
questions.explanation:
Azure Storage lifecycle management policies support block blobs and append blobs in General-purpose v2, Blob Storage, and Premium Block Blob Storage accounts. A FileStorage account is for Azure Files and does not support Blob lifecycle management policies. Therefore, the supported accounts are storage1 (StorageV2), storage2 (BlobStorage), and storage3 (BlockBlobStorage), but not storage4 (FileStorage).

**Learn more:** [Azure Blob Storage lifecycle management overview - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/lifecycle-management-overview) · [Azure Blob Storage lifecycle management policy structure - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/lifecycle-management-policy-structure)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783640509087-x5tw2sp7.png)  
  
You need to perform the tasks shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783640511595-z758f9e2.png)  
  
Which tasks can you perform by using Azure Storage Explorer?
questions.explanation:
Azure Storage Explorer can manage data-plane resources in an existing storage account, including creating file shares, uploading blobs, and working with Table storage entities. It does not create new Azure storage accounts, which is a management-plane operation typically done through the Azure portal, ARM, CLI, or PowerShell. Therefore, the supported tasks are uploading an append blob to the blob container, creating a file share in the existing storage account, and adding data to the existing table; creating a new storage account is not supported in Azure Storage Explorer.

**Learn more:** [Using Storage Explorer with Azure Files | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/storage-explorer/vs-azure-tools-storage-explorer-files) · [Quickstart: Create a table in the Azure portal - Azure Storage | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/tables/table-storage-quickstart-portal)

questions.question:
You have an Azure DNS zone named `adatum.com`.  
  
You need to delegate a subdomain named `research.adatum.com` to a different DNS server in Azure.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create an NS record named research in the adatum.com zone.
Create a PTR record named research in the adatum.com zone.
Modify the SOA record of adatum.com.
Create an A record named *.research in the adatum.com zone.

questions.explanation: DNS delegation is done in the parent zone by creating an NS record set for the child label. For `research.adatum.com`, the `adatum.com` zone must contain an NS record named `research` that identifies the authoritative name servers for that delegated subdomain. PTR records are used for reverse DNS, the SOA record does not delegate a child zone, and a wildcard A record only maps names to an IP address without transferring DNS authority.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named **Subscription1** that contains an Azure Log Analytics workspace named **Workspace1**.  
  
You need to view the error events from a table named **Event**.  
  
Which query should you run in **Workspace1**?
questions.explanation:
Azure Log Analytics queries in a workspace use Kusto Query Language (KQL). Among the options, only `search in (Event) "error"` is valid KQL syntax for searching the **Event** table for error records. The other choices use PowerShell syntax, SQL syntax, or invalid KQL/PowerShell operator combinations rather than proper Log Analytics query syntax.

**Learn more:** [Get started with log queries in Azure Monitor Logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/get-started-queries) · [find operator - Kusto](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/kusto/query/find-operator?view=microsoft-fabric)

questions.question:
You sign up for Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Premium P2.  
  
You need to add a user named [email protected] as an administrator on all the computers that will be joined to the Azure AD domain.  
  
What should you configure in Azure AD?

options.text: Device settings from the Devices blade
Providers from the MFA Server blade
User settings from the Users blade
General settings from the Groups blade

questions.explanation: In Azure AD, the setting that grants specified users local administrator rights on every Azure AD-joined device is the device-level configuration for **additional local administrators on Azure AD joined devices**. That setting is found under **Devices** in **Device settings**, so configuring Device settings is what allows `[email protected]` to become an administrator on all computers joined to Azure AD.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains a virtual network named VNet1. VNet1 includes four subnets named Gateway, Perimeter, NVA, and Production.  
  
The NVA subnet contains two network virtual appliances (NVAs) that will inspect network traffic between the Perimeter subnet and the Production subnet.  
  
You need to implement an Azure load balancer for the NVAs. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- The NVAs must run in an active-active configuration that uses automatic failover.  
- The load balancer must balance traffic to two services on the Production subnet. The services use different IP addresses.  
  
Which three actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Add two load balancing rules that have HA Ports and Floating IP enabled
Add two load balancing rules that have HA Ports enabled and Floating IP disabled
Add a frontend IP configuration, a backend pool, and a health probe
Add a frontend IP configuration, two backend pools, and a health probe

questions.explanation:
Azure Load Balancer HA Ports is the feature intended for network virtual appliances such as firewalls, and it is available on Standard Load Balancer. A backend pool plus a health probe provides active-active distribution across the two NVAs and removes an unhealthy appliance automatically. Because the inspected traffic must be balanced for two services that use different IP addresses, the load balancer uses multiple frontend IP configurations with separate load-balancing rules. For this NVA pattern, the HA Ports rules should have Floating IP enabled when multiple rules/frontends target the same NVA backend pool.

**Learn more:** [Azure Load Balancer components](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/components) · [High availability ports overview in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/load-balancer-ha-ports-overview)

questions.explanation:
A template that deploys `Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups` must be deployed at **subscription scope** because resource groups are created within a subscription, not inside an existing resource group. Microsoft Learn's subscription-deployment guidance explicitly uses subscription-scope deployment for creating resource groups, and the corresponding PowerShell cmdlet for that scope is `New-AzSubscriptionDeployment`.

**Learn more:** [Subscription deployments with ARM templates](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/templates/deploy-to-subscription) · [New-AzDeployment (Az.Resources)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.resources/new-azdeployment?view=azps-15.6.0)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Policy configured as shown in the following exhibit:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783630204628-6p36jaxm.png)  
  
What is the effect of the policy?

options.text: You are prevented from creating Azure SQL servers anywhere in Subscription 1.
You can create Azure SQL servers in ContosoRG1 only.
You are prevented from creating Azure SQL Servers in ContosoRG1 only.
You can create Azure SQL servers in any resource group within Subscription 1.

questions.explanation:
The policy assignment targets **Subscription 1** and denies the resource type **Microsoft.Sql/servers** by using the built-in **Not allowed resource types** policy. Because **ContosoRG1** is listed under the assignment's exclusion scope, that resource group is not evaluated by this policy assignment. As a result, Azure SQL servers are blocked in the rest of the subscription but are still allowed in **ContosoRG1**.

You have a Microsoft 365 tenant and an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named contoso.com.  
  
You plan to grant three users named User1, User2, and User3 access to a temporary Microsoft SharePoint document library named Library1.  
  
You need to create groups for the users. The solution must ensure that the groups are deleted automatically after 180 days.  
  
Which two groups should you create? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: a Microsoft 365 group that uses the Assigned membership type
a Security group that uses the Assigned membership type
a Microsoft 365 group that uses the Dynamic User membership type
a Security group that uses the Dynamic User membership type
a Security group that uses the Dynamic Device membership type

questions.explanation:
A 180-day automatic deletion requirement maps to a Microsoft Entra group expiration policy, and that policy applies only to Microsoft 365 groups. Microsoft 365 groups can use either Assigned membership or Dynamic User membership, so both of those group types meet the lifecycle requirement. Security groups, whether assigned or dynamic, can be used for access control, but they are not covered by the Microsoft 365 group expiration policy.

**Learn more:** [Set expiration for Microsoft 365 groups - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-lifecycle) · [Manage rules for dynamic membership groups in Microsoft Entra ID - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-dynamic-membership)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to move the blueprint files to Azure.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Generate an access key. Map a drive, and then copy the files by using File Explorer.
Use Azure Storage Explorer to copy the files.
Generate a shared access signature (SAS). Map a drive, and then copy the files by using File Explorer.

questions.explanation:
Azure Storage Explorer is the appropriate tool for interactively copying files from an on-premises system into Azure Storage. It is designed for uploading and managing data in Azure storage accounts, whereas mapping a drive through File Explorer applies to specific Azure Files SMB access scenarios, and Azure Import/Export is intended for large offline data transfers using shipped drives.

**Learn more:** [Azure Storage Explorer documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-explorer/vs-azure-tools-storage-manage-with-storage-explorer) · [Introduction to Azure Import/Export](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/import-export/storage-import-export-service)

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783637542229-0zhffn5e.png)  
  
You need to create a public Azure Standard Load Balancer.  
  
Which public IP addresses can you use?
questions.explanation: A public frontend for an Azure Standard Load Balancer must use a Standard SKU public IP address. Basic SKU public IP addresses are not supported for a Standard Load Balancer frontend. From the listed addresses, only IP3 has the Standard SKU, so it is the only valid choice.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes a storage account named storage. The storage account has a blob that stores images.  
  
Client access to storage1 is granted by using a shared access signature (SAS).  
  
You need to make sure users receive a warning when they generate a SAS with a duration greater than seven days.  
  
What should you do for storage?

options.text: Set Allow recommended upper limit for shared access signature (SAS) expiry interval to Enabled.

questions.explanation:
Azure Storage SAS expiration policies define a recommended upper validity interval. When the policy is enabled, a user who creates a SAS exceeding that interval receives a warning that includes the recommended maximum. Setting **Allow recommended upper limit for shared access signature (SAS) expiry interval** to **Enabled** provides this behavior.

**Learn more:** [Configure an expiration policy for shared access signatures (SAS) - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/sas-expiration-policy)

/>","className":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has virtual machines (VMs) hosted in Microsoft Azure. The VMs are located in a single Azure virtual network named VNet1.  
  
The company has users who work remotely. The remote workers require access to the VMs on VNet1.  
  
You need to provide access for the remote workers.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure DirectAccess on a Windows Server 2012 server VM.

questions.explanation:
A Point-to-Site (P2S) VPN is the Azure VPN Gateway option designed for individual remote users to connect securely from their client computers to an Azure virtual network. Microsoft Learn states that P2S creates a secure connection to a VNet from an individual client computer and is useful for telecommuters connecting from home or other remote locations. By contrast, Site-to-Site and Multi-Site VPNs connect entire on-premises networks to Azure, and VNet-to-VNet connects Azure virtual networks to each other.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have web apps in the West US, Central US, and East US Azure regions.  
  
You have the App Service plans shown in the following table.

You plan to create an additional App Service plan named ASP5 that will use the Linux operating system.  
  
You need to identify in which of the currently used locations you can deploy ASP5.  
  
What should you recommend?

options.text: West US, Central US, or East US

questions.explanation:
An App Service plan's operating system does not restrict which Azure region it can be created in. The older platform limitation that prevented Windows and Linux App Service plans from coexisting in the same resource group and region has been resolved for all resource groups since early 2021, and even that historical restriction was scoped to resource groups, not regions in general. Because nothing about ASP5 being a Linux plan blocks it from being placed in any of the three currently used regions, it can be deployed to West US, Central US, or East US.

**Learn more:** [Manage an App Service Plan - Azure App Service | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/app-service-plan-manage)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to deploy several Azure virtual machines (VMs) by using Azure Resource Manager (ARM) templates. You have been told that the VMs will be part of a single availability set.  
  
You must ensure that the ARM template you configure allows as many VMs as possible to remain accessible if a fabric failure or maintenance event occurs.  
  
Which value should you configure for the `platformFaultDomainCount` property?
questions.explanation:
In an Azure availability set, fault domains distribute VMs across separate groups of underlying hardware so that a rack-level or fabric-related failure impacts only the VMs in one fault domain. Increasing the fault domain count improves resilience to such failures because more VMs can remain running in other domains. Microsoft documents `platformFaultDomainCount` as the number of fault domains for the availability set, and using the maximum supported value provides the greatest protection against fabric failure.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft.Compute/availabilitySets - ARM template reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.compute/availabilitysets) · [Availability options for Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/availability)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure AD tenant named adatum.com that contains the groups shown in the following table.

You assign the Azure Active Directory Premium Plan 2 license to Group1 and User4.  
  
Which users receive the Azure Active Directory Premium Plan 2 license?
questions.explanation: In Azure AD group-based licensing, licenses assigned to a group apply to that group's direct user members, but nested groups are not processed for license assignment. Because Group1 is licensed, User1 receives the license as a direct member of Group1. User2 and User3 do not receive it through Group2 and Group3 because nested group membership is not supported for group-based licensing. User4 receives the license because it is assigned directly.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two Azure subscriptions named **Sub1** and **Sub2**.

You need to move **VM1** to **Sub2**.  
  
Which resources should you move to **Sub2**?
questions.explanation:
An Azure virtual machine can be moved to another subscription only together with all of its required dependent resources. For this VM, the required dependencies are the managed OS disk (**Disk1**) and the network interface (**NetInt1**). Because the NIC is connected to a subnet in **VNet1**, the virtual network must also move when moving the VM across subscriptions. **storage1** is not required because the VM uses a managed disk resource, not a storage-account-hosted unmanaged disk.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two subscriptions named Subscription1 and Subscription2. Each subscription is linked to a different Azure AD tenant.

You need to connect VNet1 to VNet2.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Modify the IP address space of VNet2.

questions.explanation: To connect virtual networks across different subscriptions and Azure AD tenants, virtual network gateways must be provisioned on each VNet. The given IP address spaces (10.0.0.0/16 and 10.10.0.0/24) do not overlap, so IP space modification is unnecessary. Moving resources between subscriptions or modifying VNet configuration is not required. VPN gateways enable secure VNet-to-VNet connections across subscription and tenant boundaries.

questions.question:
Solution: From Azure CLI, you run `azcopy`.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation: `azcopy` is used to transfer data to and from Azure Storage services, not to apply Kubernetes manifest files to an Azure Kubernetes Service cluster. To deploy a YAML file to AKS, you would typically use `kubectl apply -f <file>` after connecting to the cluster, for example by retrieving credentials with Azure CLI. Because `azcopy` does not deploy resources to Kubernetes, this solution does not meet the requirement.

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question:
Solution: From Azure Cloud Shell, you run `az aks`.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Deploying a YAML manifest to Azure Kubernetes Service requires using Kubernetes tooling such as `kubectl apply -f` against the cluster after connecting with `az aks get-credentials`. The `az aks` command is only the Azure CLI command group for AKS management and, by itself, does not deploy a YAML file to the cluster. Microsoft Learn documents `az aks get-credentials` for configuring access to AKS and then using `kubectl` to work with cluster resources.\
\
**Learn more:** [az aks | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/aks?view=azure-cli-latest) · [Quickstart: Deploy an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster using Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/learn/quick-kubernetes-deploy-cli)

For Windows point-to-site VPN clients, Azure supports connectivity to directly peered virtual networks, but when virtual network peering or network topology changes are made, the point-to-site VPN client package must be downloaded again so the client receives the new routes.
