questions.question:
You have the Azure virtual networks shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783630316090-3hkvdplf.png)  
  
From VNet1, to which virtual networks can you create a peering connection?
questions.explanation: Azure virtual network peering is supported only between virtual networks whose address spaces do not overlap. VNet2 cannot be peered with VNet1 because VNet2's 10.11.0.0/17 range overlaps with VNet1's 10.11.0.0/16 range. VNet3 (10.10.0.0/22) and VNet4 (192.168.16.0/22) do not overlap with VNet1, and Azure supports peering both within a region and across regions by using global virtual network peering.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named **Subscription1** that has the following providers registered:  
  
- Authorization  
- Automation  
- Resources  
- Compute  
- KeyVault  
- Network  
- Storage  
- Billing  
- Web  
  
Subscription1 contains an Azure virtual machine named **VM1** that has the following configurations:  
  
- Private IP address: **10.0.0.4 (dynamic)**  
- Network security group (NSG): **NSG1**  
- Public IP address: **None**  
- Availability set: **AVSet**  
- Subnet: **10.0.0.0/24**  
- Managed disks: **No**  
- Location: **East US**  
  
You need to record all successful and failed connection attempts to **VM1**.  
  
Which **three** actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Enable Azure Network Watcher in the East US Azure region.
Add an Azure Network Watcher connection monitor.
Enable Azure Network Watcher flow logs.

questions.explanation:
Recording successful and failed connection attempts to the VM is done with Azure Network Watcher flow logs on the network security group that filters the VM's traffic. Flow logs require the **Microsoft.Insights** resource provider to be registered, and the logs are written to an **Azure Storage account**. You must then **enable Azure Network Watcher flow logs** for the NSG. A connection monitor tests connectivity paths but does not capture every allowed and denied NSG traffic decision for the VM.

**Learn more:** [Create, change, enable, disable, or delete NSG flow logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/nsg-flow-logs-manage) · [NSG Flow Logs Overview - Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/nsg-flow-logs-overview)

questions.question:
You plan to deploy several Azure virtual machines running Windows Server 2022 in a virtual machine scale set by using an Azure Resource Manager template.  
  
You need to make sure that NGINX is available on every virtual machine after deployment.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: Deployment Center in Azure App Service

questions.explanation:
Azure Custom Script Extension runs post-deployment scripts on Azure virtual machines, including Windows Server 2022 instances in a virtual machine scale set. Declaring the extension in the Azure Resource Manager template lets each instance download and run an installation script, ensuring NGINX is installed as instances are deployed.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Custom Script Extension for Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/extensions/custom-script-windows)

questions.question:
You plan to deploy several Azure virtual machines running Windows Server 2022 in a virtual machine scale set by using an Azure Resource Manager template.  
  
You need to make sure that NGINX is available on every virtual machine after deployment.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
The minimum is two App Service plans because apps can share a plan only when they are compatible with the same underlying App Service environment, especially the operating system. ASP.NET 4.8 requires Windows, and Azure App Service supports .NET and PHP on Windows, so those apps can be placed together on one Windows plan. Python 3.11 on Azure App Service requires Linux, so it must be placed on a separate Linux plan.

**Learn more:** [Operating system functionality in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/overview-operating-systems) · [Configure a Linux Python app for Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/configure-language-python)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains the virtual networks shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783646930581-nekn7hqy.png)  
  
You need to ensure that all traffic between VNet1 and VNet2 traverses the Microsoft backbone network.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Azure virtual network peering, specifically global VNet peering for VNets in different regions, provides direct connectivity between VNet1 and VNet2 over the Microsoft backbone network. Microsoft Learn states that traffic between virtual machines in peered virtual networks is routed directly through the Microsoft backbone infrastructure, not over the public internet. Private endpoints connect a VNet to a specific Azure service, ExpressRoute is for private connectivity with on-premises networks, and route tables do not establish VNet-to-VNet connectivity by themselves.

**Learn more:** [Azure Virtual Network Peering | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-peering-overview) · [Create, Change, or Delete Azure Virtual Network Peering | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-manage-peering)

options.text: Create a network security group (NSG) that has an outbound security rule to deny destination port 3389 and apply the NSG to the network interface of VM1.
Create a network security group (NSG) that has an outbound security rule to deny source port 3389 and apply the NSG to Subnet1.
Create a network security group (NSG) that has an inbound security rule to deny source port 3389 and apply the NSG to Subnet1.

questions.explanation:
An Azure network security group can deny outbound traffic from a virtual machine's network interface or subnet, and NSG rules match on direction plus source and destination details, including the destination port. To block VM1 from making an RDP connection to VM2, the rule must deny **outbound** traffic from VM1 to **destination port 3389**. Using source port 3389 is incorrect because client-initiated RDP sessions normally use an ephemeral source port, while 3389 is the destination port on the target VM. Azure Bastion does not enforce this VM-to-VM traffic block. Official Microsoft documentation describes NSGs as filtering inbound and outbound traffic and specifies destinationPortRange and sourcePortRange as separate rule properties.

You have an Azure subscription that contains the virtual networks shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783645849445-q41emxbf.png)  
  
The subscription contains the virtual machines shown in the following table.

All the virtual machines have only private IP addresses.  
  
You deploy an Azure Bastion host named Bastion1 to VNet1.  
  
To which virtual machines can you connect by using Bastion1?
questions.explanation:
Azure Bastion provides RDP/SSH access to VMs in the same virtual network as the Bastion host and in directly peered virtual networks, including global peering across regions. Because Bastion1 is deployed in VNet1, it can reach VM1 in VNet1 and VM2 in VNet2, which is directly peered with VNet1. It cannot reach VM3 in VNet3 through VNet2 because virtual network peering is not transitive, so VNet3 is not a peered network of VNet1 for Bastion access.

**Learn more:** [VNet peering and Azure Bastion architecture | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bastion/vnet-peering) · [Tutorial: Connect virtual networks with virtual network peering | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/tutorial-connect-virtual-networks)
